title: Acaraje black-eyed pea fritters with shrimp filling
steps: For the filling, blend half of the red onion with the ginger, the red chili and a pinch of salt until smooth.

Heat the 1 tbsp of oil in a frying pan and fry the paste for about 5 minutes. Add the shrimp, the chopped tomatoes and the cilantro, squeeze in the lime and season with salt. Cook for 3 minutes, until the shrimp are pink, then take it off the heat.
For the fritters, drain and rinse the black-eyed peas, then blend them with the garlic and the green chili until smooth.
Scrape the purée into a bowl and mix in the rest of the onion (finely chopped), the flour, salt, chili powder and baking powder. Roll the mixture into 16 balls.
Heat about 3 inches (8 cm) of oil in a wok or deep pan. When a small piece of bread sizzles in it, fry 4 or 5 balls at a time for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Split each fritter open, spoon in some of the shrimp filling and serve with hot sauce.

title: Air fryer patatas bravas
steps: Cut the potatoes into chunks, cover them with just-boiled water and let them soak for 30 minutes. Drain and let them dry for 5 minutes.
Heat the air fryer to 400°F (200°C). Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp of the oil and 1/2 tsp each of salt and black pepper, then air-fry them for 20 to 30 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, heat the rest of the oil in a small pan over medium-low heat and cook the chopped onion for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft but not brown.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the paprika for 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, add the canned tomatoes and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, until slightly thicker.
Pile the potatoes on a plate, spoon the sauce over them and scatter with basil.

title: Ajo blanco
steps: Tear the bread into a bowl, pour 1 1/2 cups (350 ml) of water over it and let it soak for 10 minutes.
Put the bread and its water in a blender with the almonds, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, another 1 1/2 cups (350 ml) of water and 1 tsp of salt. Blend until very smooth.
Chill the soup for about 1 hour. Serve it cold with a drizzle of olive oil and some black pepper.

title: Algerian Carrots
steps: Slice the carrots. Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan with a steamer basket, add the carrots, cover and steam over medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes, until just tender. Keep 1/2 cup of the cooking water.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over low heat with the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, minced garlic and thyme. Cook gently for about 10 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant.
Pour in the saved cooking water, add the bay leaf, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the carrots and heat them through for 2 to 3 minutes. Remove the bay leaf, sprinkle with the lemon juice and serve.

title: Algerian Flafla (Bell Pepper Salad)
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Roast the whole peppers on a sheet of foil for 30 to 45 minutes, turning them once, until the skins are blackened and the peppers are soft.
Let them cool for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins, remove the stems and seeds and cut the peppers into 1/2-inch pieces.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onion for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, salt and pepper, then the peppers and the chopped tomato. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomato is soft. Serve warm or cold.

title: Algerian Kefta (Meatballs)
steps: Mix the ground beef with half of the minced garlic and 1 tbsp of the chopped onion, using your hands. Shape it into 12 to 14 small oval patties, about 1 1/2 inches long.
Brown the patties in batches in a large skillet over medium-high heat, about 10 minutes, until crisp outside and cooked through. Set them aside in a serving dish.
Lower the heat to medium, add the rest of the onion to the pan, season with salt and pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, until soft. Add the rest of the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes and the parsley, pour in the water and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft. Pour the sauce over the meatballs and serve.

title: Antiguan Breakfast (Chop Up and ‘Saltfish’)
steps: Peel the eggplants and the pumpkin and cut them into medium pieces.
Melt the butter in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Cook the chopped onion and garlic for 2 minutes, until soft but not brown.
Add the pumpkin and eggplant and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. Pour in water just to cover, bring to a boil, then simmer for about 15 minutes, until the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the chopped callaloo and cook for 3 minutes.
Drain the vegetables in a colander, return them to the pot and mash them well. Season with the salt and pepper and serve.

title: Arepa
steps: Put the masarepa (precooked corn flour) in a bowl. Dissolve the salt in the warm water and add it little by little, mixing, until you have a soft dough. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Shape the dough into rounds about 3 inches wide and 1/2 inch thick.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Cook the arepas slowly in a lightly oiled skillet until a crust forms on both sides.
Bake them for about 20 minutes, until they sound hollow when tapped.

title: Arroz con gambas y calamar
steps: Peel and devein most of the shrimp, keeping a few whole to decorate if you like. Clean the squid and slice it into rings.

Heat the oil in a large frying pan or shallow casserole over medium-low heat and cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the bay leaf, saffron, rice and tomato paste and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the seafood stock and 2/3 cup (150 ml) of water. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the squid, season well and bring to a boil. Cover, lower the heat and simmer gently for 12 minutes, adding a splash of water if it looks dry.
Stir in the peeled shrimp and lay any whole ones on top. Cover and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes more, until the shrimp are pink. Let it stand for 2 minutes, then serve from the pan.

title: Asado
steps: Light a charcoal or wood grill and let it burn down to glowing coals. Without a grill, heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) instead.
Salt the beef generously just before cooking.

Grill the beef with the thickest cuts farthest from the heat, turning now and then, until it's cooked the way you like it. Thin cuts take about 20 minutes and ribs up to 2 hours. In the oven, roast the beef on a rack.
Add the chorizo and morcilla for the last 20 to 30 minutes, turning them until browned and cooked through.
Let the meat rest for 10 minutes, then slice it. Serve with chimichurri, a tomato salad and crusty bread.

title: Aubergine & hummus grills
steps: Heat the broiler. Slice the eggplants, lay them in one layer on a large baking sheet, brush them lightly with the vegetable oil and season well.
Broil for about 15 minutes, turning twice and brushing with oil, until soft and cooked through. Meanwhile, blend the bread into crumbs, add 2 tsp of oil and pulse briefly to coat.
Spread a couple of teaspoons of hummus on each slice and press the hummus side into the crumbs. Broil crumb side up for about 3 minutes, until golden.
Toss the chopped walnuts, parsley and halved tomatoes with the lemon juice, olive oil and seasoning, and serve with the eggplant and more hummus.

title: Aubergine couscous salad
steps: Heat the broiler to high. Cut the eggplant into thick slices, lay them on a baking sheet, brush with oil and season.
Broil for about 15 minutes, turning and brushing with more oil halfway, until browned and soft.
Meanwhile, put the couscous in a large bowl, pour the hot broth over it, cover and leave for 10 minutes.
Mix the halved tomatoes, chopped mint, crumbled goat cheese and the rest of the oil.
Fluff the couscous with a fork, then stir in the eggplant, the tomato mixture and the lemon juice.

title: Aussie Burgers
steps: Put the beef in a bowl with 1 tsp of salt and plenty of black pepper. With wet hands, mix it and shape it into 4 burgers.
Slice the beets and split each naan in half.
Heat a grill pan over high heat. Toast the naan halves on both sides and set them aside.
Cook the burgers for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, or until cooked through.
Put a naan half on each plate with some arugula, then a burger, a few slices of beet and a spoonful of the sour cream dip. Season and serve.

title: Ayam Percik
steps: Blend the shallots, ginger, garlic, chilies, turmeric, cumin, coriander seeds and fennel seeds into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in a skillet over medium heat for 10 minutes, until fragrant, adding a spoonful of water or oil if it gets too dry. Don't let it burn.
Add the tamarind paste, coconut milk, water, sugar and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly reduced. Let it cool.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and marinate it in the fridge overnight, or for up to 2 days.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Spread some of the marinade on a greased baking sheet, lay the chicken on top so it covers the sauce, and spread the rest over the chicken.
Roast for 35 to 45 minutes, until cooked through (175°F inside). Let it rest for 5 minutes and serve with the sauce and steamed rice.

title: Bahia-style Moqueca prawn stew
steps: Mix the shrimp with 2 tbsp of the lime juice, 1 tsp of salt and 1 tbsp of the chopped garlic. Chill for 1 hour.
Heat the coconut oil in a large saucepan and cook the green onions and onion for 5 minutes. Add the sliced red pepper, pepper flakes, paprika and the rest of the garlic.
Add the chopped tomatoes, coconut milk and a little salt. Simmer for 10 minutes to thicken.
Add the shrimp with their marinade and the rest of the lime juice. Simmer gently for about 3 minutes, until the shrimp turn pink. Serve with the cilantro and rice.

title: Baingan Bharta
steps: Rub the eggplant with a little oil and roast it directly over a gas flame, turning it every 2 to 3 minutes, until the skin is charred and the inside is completely soft (a knife slides in easily). You can also roast it in a hot oven, with less smoky flavor.
Let it cool in a bowl of water, then peel off the skin and chop or mash the flesh.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the chopped onion and garlic until soft and translucent, without browning. Add the chopped green chili for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook, stirring, until the oil starts to separate from the mixture. Stir in the chili powder.
Add the eggplant, season with salt and cook for 4 to 5 minutes more, stirring well. Stir in the cilantro and serve with roti, chapati or rice.

title: Baked salmon with fennel & tomatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Trim the fennel, keeping the fronds. Cut each bulb in half and each half into 3 wedges.
Boil the fennel in salted water for 10 minutes and drain it well. Chop the fronds and mix them with the parsley and the lemon zest.
Spread the fennel in a shallow baking dish with the tomatoes, drizzle with the oil and bake for 10 minutes.
Nestle the salmon among the vegetables, sprinkle with lemon juice and bake for 15 minutes more, until the fish is just cooked.
Scatter the herb mixture over the top, add the olives if you like, and serve.

title: Baked Yuca Fries
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Trim the yuca, cut each one in half across and cut off the waxy peel. Cut each piece lengthwise into quarters (16 pieces in all) and remove the woody center.
Boil the yuca for 8 to 10 minutes, until a fork goes in easily. Drain and pat dry.
Toss with the oil, chili powder, salt and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet and bake for about 25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, blend the avocado, sour cream, lime juice and cilantro until smooth, and season. Serve the fries hot with the sauce.

title: Balchi di Pisca
steps: A day ahead, soak the salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, then drain it.
Cover the cod with fresh water and simmer gently for about 15 minutes, until it flakes easily. Drain, keeping a little of the cooking water, and remove any bones.
Peel and dice the potatoes, boil them until tender and drain them well. Mash them with the cod.
Blend the chopped tomato, green pepper, onion and garlic with the hot sauce, a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper for a few seconds. Mix it into the fish with the beaten egg.
The mixture should be firm enough to shape: add a spoonful of the cooking water if it's too dry. Roll it into balls about 1 1/2 inches wide.
Deep-fry the balls in hot oil until golden brown, then drain them on paper towels.

title: Bangladeshi fish curry with daikon
steps: Cut the fish into 2 1/2-inch chunks, rinse and drain. Peel the daikon, cut it lengthwise into quarters and slice it into 3/4-inch (2 cm) pieces. Blend the onion into a paste.
Heat the oil in a large, shallow pan over medium heat. Fry the crushed garlic for 1 minute, until pale golden.
Add the onion paste and salt and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until soft. Pour in 3/4 cup (200 ml) of water, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, coriander and chili powder for 2 minutes, then cover and cook over low heat for 5 minutes.
Add the daikon and another 3/4 cup (200 ml) of water. Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add the fish and gently coat it in the sauce. Cover and cook for 5 minutes. From now on, shake the pan instead of stirring, so the fish doesn't break.

Pour 2 cups (500 ml) of hot water down the side of the pan, cover and simmer for 15 minutes. Add the cilantro and the sliced green chilies, cook for 5 minutes more and serve with rice and lime wedges.

title: Barramundi with Moroccan spices
steps: Blend the cumin, coriander, paprika, chili powder, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, cilantro and a pinch of salt into a dressing.
Cut three slashes on each side of the fish, coat it with half of the dressing and let it marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Roast the fish on a tray for 20 minutes, until the flesh is firm.
Serve with the rest of the dressing and couscous or rice.

title: Beef Banh Mi Bowls with Sriracha Mayo, Carrot & Pickled Cucumber
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs clear. Put it in a small pot with 2 cups of water and a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes. Keep it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, chop the garlic, zest the lime and cut it into wedges, slice the cucumber into thin half-moons, dice the onion and grate the carrot.
Mix the cucumber with the juice of half the lime, 1/2 tsp of sugar and a pinch of salt. Mix the mayonnaise with a pinch of the garlic, a squeeze of lime and as much sriracha as you like.

Heat a little oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes. Add the beef, the garlic and 4 tsp of sugar and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned. Stir in the soy sauce and season.
Fluff the rice and stir in the lime zest. Divide it between bowls and top with the beef, carrot and cucumber, a squeeze of lime and the sriracha mayo.

title: Beef Bourguignon
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the goose fat in a large casserole. Season the beef and brown it on all sides, 3 to 5 minutes per side, in 2 or 3 batches. Set it aside in a colander over a bowl.
In the same pan, fry the bacon, shallots, mushrooms, garlic and bouquet garni until lightly browned. Stir in the tomato paste for a few minutes, then return the beef and its juices.
Pour in the wine and about 1/2 cup (100 ml) of water, so the meat is almost covered. Bring to a boil, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom.

Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Cover the stew with a sheet of foil pressed onto its surface and cook in the oven for 3 hours. If the sauce is thin, lift out the meat and vegetables and boil the sauce for a few minutes to thicken it.

For the mash, peel and cube the celeriac. Fry it in the olive oil for 5 minutes, until golden, and season. Add the rosemary, thyme, 1 bay leaf and the cardamom pods, pour in about 3/4 cup (200 ml) of water, partly cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes.
Drain any water left, remove the herbs and cardamom, and crush the celeriac with a masher and a little olive oil. Serve the stew in bowls with the mash on top.

title: Beef Brisket Pot Roast
steps: Trim any large chunks of fat from the brisket, keeping a thin layer on one side. Score that fat in a criss-cross pattern, cutting through the fat but not the meat. Salt the brisket well and leave it at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Pat it dry and put it fat side down in a heavy, ovenproof pot over medium-high heat. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, until the fat is browned, then turn it and brown the other side. Set it aside.
Add the chopped onions to the fat in the pot with a little salt and cook over high heat for 5 to 8 minutes, until lightly browned. Stir in the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes.

Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Tie the bay leaves, rosemary and thyme together. Put the brisket back in the pot with the onions around it, add the broth and the herbs and bring to a boil on the stove.
Cover and cook in the oven for 3 hours, turning the brisket every hour. Add the carrots and cook for 1 hour more, until the meat is falling-apart tender.

Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender. Move the brisket to a board, cover it with foil and remove the herbs. If you like, blend half of the onions and the cooking liquid with the mustard into a gravy.
Slice the meat across the grain and serve with the carrots, onions, potatoes and gravy.

title: Beef Empanadas
steps: For the dough, stir the lard, warm water and salt in a large bowl. Add the flour and half of the oregano and knead for 5 minutes. Cover and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Hard-boil the eggs, then peel and dice them. Put the tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds, cool them, peel them and dice them.
Cook the crushed garlic and the diced onions in a little oil until soft, then set them aside. Dice the steak and brown it in the same pan over high heat.

Season the meat with the rest of the oregano, the paprika, pepper flakes and parsley, add the onions, garlic, tomatoes and green onions and simmer for a few minutes. Season with salt and pepper and stir in the eggs.

Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface and cut 5-inch (12 cm) circles. Put 2 to 4 teaspoons of filling on each, wet the edges, fold into half-moons and seal with a fork.
Brush with the egg wash and bake on a lined baking sheet for about 25 minutes, until golden. Serve warm with chimichurri.

title: BEEF LOK LAK (Lok Lak Sach Ko)
steps: Fry the eggs sunny side up and set them aside. Chop the garlic, wash and dry the lettuce, and thinly slice the onion and tomatoes.
Cut the beef into 1-inch (2 to 3 cm) cubes and mix it with the salt, palm sugar, wine, oyster sauce, soy sauce and sesame oil.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat and fry the garlic until lightly browned. Add the beef with all of its marinade and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, depending on how rare you like it.
Toast the peppercorns in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, grind them and mix them with a pinch of salt and the lime juice for a dipping sauce.
Arrange the lettuce, tomatoes and onion on a plate, spoon the beef on top and finish with the fried eggs. Serve with the pepper sauce and steamed rice.

title: Beef Mechado
steps: Cut the beef into 2-inch cubes and the potato into large chunks.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the crushed garlic and chopped onion until soft.
Add the beef and brown it on all sides.

Stir in the soy sauce, a squeeze of the lemon, the tomato paste, the water and the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for about 1 hour 15 minutes, until the beef is tender. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Add the potato and cook for 15 minutes more, until tender. Season with the pepper and salt and serve with rice.

title: Beef pumpkin Stew
steps: Cut the beef into 1-inch chunks and toss them in the flour until coated on all sides.
Melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in small batches and set it aside in a bowl.
Add the onion and garlic to the pot and cook for 1 minute, scraping the bottom as you stir.
Return the beef and add the broth, pumpkin purée, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium-low and simmer for 3 hours, stirring now and then.
Add the cubed potatoes, sliced carrots and thyme sprigs, turn the heat up to medium and cook for 30 minutes more. Season to taste and serve.

title: Beef stroganoff
steps: Heat the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan and cook the sliced onion over medium heat for about 15 minutes, until very soft, adding a splash of water if it sticks.
Add the crushed garlic for 2 to 3 minutes, then the butter. When it foams, add the sliced mushrooms and cook for about 5 minutes, until soft. Season and tip everything onto a plate.
Season the flour with a big pinch of salt and pepper and toss the sliced steak in it. Fry the steak for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned, adding a little oil if the pan is dry.
Return the onions and mushrooms. Whisk the crème fraîche, mustard and broth together, pour them in and cook over medium heat for about 5 minutes.
Scatter with parsley and serve with pasta or rice.

title: Beef Wellington
steps: Pulse the mushrooms with some salt and pepper in a food processor into a rough paste. Cook it in a pan over high heat for about 10 minutes, stirring often, until dry. Let it cool.
Season the beef and sear it in a hot pan with a little olive oil for 30 seconds on each side, just to brown it. Let it cool, then brush it all over with the mustard.

Lay the prosciutto slices on a sheet of plastic wrap, slightly overlapping. Spread the mushroom paste over them and put the beef in the middle. Using the plastic wrap, roll the ham tightly around the beef and twist the ends. Chill for 15 to 20 minutes.

Roll out the pastry on a floured surface into a large rectangle. Unwrap the beef and lay it in the center. Brush the pastry around it with egg yolk, fold the ends over and wrap the pastry around the beef, cutting off any excess.
Put it seam side down on a baking sheet, brush with egg yolk and chill for about 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).

Score the pastry lightly, brush it with egg yolk again and bake for 20 minutes. Lower the oven to 350°F (180°C) and bake for 15 minutes more. Let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes before slicing. The beef should still be pink in the middle.

title: Beetroot latkes
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Grate the beets and mix them with the egg, flour, crushed garlic, caraway, cumin, lemon zest and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan and spoon in the mixture to make 6 round latkes. Fry them for 4 to 5 minutes on each side.
Move them to a baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.
Mix the yogurt with the chopped mint. Toss the arugula and halved tomatoes with a squeeze of lemon, and serve with the latkes and the mint yogurt.

title: Belgian Meatballs in Liège Syrup Sauce
steps: Mix the beef and pork with 1 finely chopped onion, the garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, 1 tbsp of the mustard, the parsley, salt and pepper. Shape into meatballs, as small or as large as you like.
Heat a little oil in a large pan and brown the meatballs on all sides. Set them aside.
Melt the butter in the same pan and cook the other 2 onions, sliced, until soft and lightly golden. Sprinkle in the brown sugar and let it melt.

Add the vinegar and scrape up the browned bits. Stir in the rest of the mustard and the Liège syrup, then pour in the broth (and a splash of beer if you like) and add the bay leaf. Stir until the sauce is glossy.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens. Taste and adjust, and serve with fries or mashed potatoes.

title: Belgian Waterzooi Chicken
steps: Put the chicken, water and 1 garlic clove in a large saucepan and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
When the chicken is cool, dice the breast and pull the meat off the leg, without skin or bones. Cut the leeks, celery and carrot into thin strips and dice the potatoes.
Melt the butter with the rosemary and bay leaves in a large pan over medium heat. Add the vegetables, season with salt and pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken, cover and cook for 5 minutes. Pour in the cream and 1/2 cup (120 ml) of the broth, cover and cook for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Whisk the egg yolk with 2 tbsp of the warm cream from the pan, stir it back in over very low heat to thicken the sauce, and remove the herbs. Season and serve hot.

title: Bengali Chicken Curry with Potatoes
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chopped onions for about 5 minutes, until translucent. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for 5 minutes more.
Lower the heat to medium, add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until pulpy. Stir in the cayenne, curry powder, garam masala, turmeric and cumin and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the diced chicken and potatoes and simmer, stirring now and then, for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Sprinkle with the cilantro, simmer for 10 minutes more and serve hot.

title: Bitterballen (Dutch meatballs)
steps: Melt the butter in a pan and stir in half of the flour, little by little, into a thick paste. Slowly stir in the broth until smooth, then simmer over low heat for a couple of minutes.
Stir in the finely chopped onion, the parsley and the cooked, shredded beef, and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. It should become a very thick sauce.
Spread it in a shallow container, cover and chill for several hours, until firm.

Roll heaped tablespoons of the mixture into small balls. Roll each one in the rest of the flour, then in the beaten eggs, then in the breadcrumbs, making sure the egg covers it completely. Chill them while the oil heats.
Heat oil for deep-frying to 375°F (190°C) and fry 4 balls at a time until golden. Serve with a grainy mustard.

title: Black bean & meat stew - feijoada
steps: Soak the black beans in cold water overnight, then drain them.

Fry the bacon in a large heavy pan with a lid until crisp, then lift it out, keeping the fat. Brown the ribs, sliced chorizo and cubed pork shoulder in batches, seasoning each batch, and set them aside.
Add the chopped onions, garlic and pepper flakes to the pan, with a little oil if needed. Season and cook for 8 minutes, until soft.
Return all the meat and add the bay leaves and beans. Pour in just enough water to cover, about 2 3/4 cups (650 ml), and bring to a boil.

Cover and simmer over low heat for 2 hours, until the beans are soft and the meat is tender. If there's too much liquid, take the lid off for the last hour. Serve with rice, chopped parsley, hot sauce and orange slices.

title: Black Beans Hotpot
steps: Soak the dried beans in cold water overnight, then drain them.
Put the beans in a large pot with the chopped onion, bell peppers, celery and garlic, the cumin, oregano, salt, pepper and water.

Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 1 1/2 hours, until the beans are very soft. Add more water if they get dry. (In a pressure cooker, cook on high for 35 minutes and let the pressure release on its own.)
Taste, adjust the seasoning and serve.

title: Blini Pancakes
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour, all-purpose flour, salt and yeast in a large bowl. Make a well in the middle and whisk in the warm milk until smooth.
Cover and let the batter rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Separate the egg. Stir 2 tbsp of the butter (melted) and the egg yolk into the batter. Whisk the egg white until stiff and fold it in gently. Cover and let it stand for 20 minutes.
Heat a little butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Drop in small spoonfuls of batter and cook for about 1 minute, until bubbles form, then turn and cook for 30 seconds more.
Keep the blini warm under a towel while you cook the rest, adding more butter to the pan as needed.

title: Bolani with Potato Filling
steps: Mix the flour and 1 tsp of the salt in a bowl and slowly add the water to make a stiff dough. Knead for 5 to 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Cover with a damp cloth and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water until soft. Drain and mash them well, then mix in the chopped green onions, the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Divide the dough into 3 or 4 balls and roll each one out as thin as you can on a floured surface. Cut out 5 to 6-inch (13 to 15 cm) circles.
Spread 1 to 2 tablespoons of potato over each circle, wet the edges, fold them over and press to seal.
Shallow-fry the bolani 1 or 2 at a time in hot oil until browned on both sides. Keep them warm until all are done and serve right away.

title: Borsch
steps: For the broth, put the beef, 1 whole onion, the bay leaf and 8 cups (2 liters) of lightly salted cold water in a large saucepan. Simmer over very low heat for about 1 1/2 hours, until the beef falls apart, skimming the top now and then. Break up the beef and remove the onion.
Add the diced potatoes, season well and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until tender.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a deep frying pan and cook the other onion and the carrot, both diced, over medium heat until soft. Add the grated beets and cook for about 5 minutes, then the diced red pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chopped prunes, turn up the heat and boil to reduce slightly, then stir everything into the soup.
Add the shredded cabbage and the beans and cook for 7 to 10 minutes, until tender. Serve with a spoonful of crème fraîche, plenty of chopped dill and crusty bread.

title: Boulangère Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Thinly slice the onions and the potatoes.
Fry the onions and thyme sprigs in the oil for about 5 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Oil a 6-cup (1.5 liter) baking dish. Layer the potatoes with a few onions between each layer, finishing with potatoes.
Pour the broth over the top and bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until the potatoes are cooked and the top is golden and crisp.

title: Braised Beef Chilli
steps: Heat the oven to 250°F (120°C). Take the beef out of the fridge. Pulse the onions and garlic in a food processor until finely chopped.
Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large casserole and brown the beef on all sides. Set it aside, add a little more oil and brown the sliced chorizo, then set it aside too.
Cook the onion and garlic with the cumin, allspice, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, oregano and ancho chilies in the chorizo oil until soft. Season and stir in the vinegar, tomatoes, ketchup and sugar.
Return the meat with 1 2/3 cups (400 ml) of water (or red wine), bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours.
Add the drained beans and cook for 1 hour more. Pull the meat apart with two forks just before serving.

title: Braised stuffed cabbage
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Cut the tough stalk out of the cabbage leaves. Cook them in boiling salted water for 1 to 2 minutes, until they start to wilt, then cool them under cold water and pat dry.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes, until lightly browned. Add the rosemary and the chopped celery and cook for 8 minutes more.
Stir in the rice for about 1 minute, until glossy. Take it off the heat, stir in the chopped chestnuts and the cranberries and season.
Spoon some of the filling onto each leaf, fold in the sides and roll it up. Put the rolls seam side down in a single layer in an oiled baking dish.
Mix the broth, vinegar and honey and pour it over. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour, then uncover and bake for 15 minutes more.

title: Breaded Steak Recipe (Lomo de Res Apanado)
steps: Put each piece of steak between two sheets of plastic and pound it with a mallet until it's 1/4 to 1/2 inch thick.
Put the steaks in a dish with the aliños sauce and marinate in the fridge for 3 hours or overnight.
Mix the flour, breadcrumbs, cumin, parsley, salt and pepper on a plate, and beat the eggs in a bowl.
Coat each steak in the flour mixture, then the egg, then the flour mixture again.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat until it just starts to smoke. Fry the steaks for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until golden, then drain them on paper towels and serve.

title: Breadfruit in Butter Sauce
steps: Cut the breadfruit, remove the core and seeds and peel it. Boil it in salted water with a piece of onion and a little oil until tender, then drain and let it cool.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a frying pan and lightly brown the onions, sliced into rings.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, parsley, lime juice, salt and pepper and cook for a couple of minutes. Pour in the water, bring to a boil and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes.
Slice the breadfruit into a serving dish, pour the butter sauce over it and add pepper sauce to taste. Garnish with chopped parsley.

title: Breakfast Potatoes
steps: Dice the potatoes and keep them in a bowl of water so they don't brown. Chop the bacon (it's easier if you freeze it for a few minutes first).
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Drain the potatoes, add them to the pan and season with salt, pepper and a pinch of allspice.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until browned, adding a little more oil if needed.
Add the bacon and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until crisp. Lower the heat to medium-low, add the minced garlic and parsley and cook for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Drizzle the maple syrup over the potatoes, toss and cook for 1 minute more. Serve warm.

title: Broccoli & Stilton soup
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and cook the chopped onion over medium heat until soft, adding a splash of water if it starts to stick.
Add the chopped celery, leek and potato and the butter. Stir until the butter melts, then cover and let the vegetables sweat for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth, add the chopped broccoli stalk and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until everything is soft.
Add the broccoli florets and cook for 5 minutes more. Blend until smooth, then stir in the crumbled Stilton, leaving a few lumps. Season with black pepper and serve.

title: Brown Stew Chicken
steps: Cut the chicken into pieces. Squeeze the lime over it, rub it in well and drain off the juice.
Mix the chicken in a large bowl with the chopped tomato, onions, garlic and red pepper, the thyme, allspice and soy sauce. Cover and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot. Lift the chicken out of the marinade, shaking off the vegetables, and keep the marinade. Brown the chicken a few pieces at a time in the very hot oil.
Drain off the extra oil and return all the chicken. Pour in the marinade, add the sliced carrot and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Mix the cornstarch into the coconut milk and stir it into the stew. Turn the heat to low and cook for 20 minutes more, until the chicken is tender.

title: Bulgarian Green Salad
steps: Slice the lettuce into a large bowl and add the sliced radishes, cucumber and green onions.
Drizzle with the vinegar and olive oil, season with salt and toss gently.
Scatter with chopped dill and parsley and serve right away.

title: Cabbage Soup (Shchi)
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy pot over medium heat and cook the chopped onion until translucent.
Add the shredded cabbage and the chopped carrot and celery and cook for about 3 minutes, stirring often, until they start to soften.
Add the bay leaf and broth and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over low heat for about 15 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes, bring back to a boil and simmer, covered, for about 10 minutes, until tender.
Add the chopped tomatoes, bring back to a boil and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and remove the bay leaf.
Serve topped with sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Cabbage with Ground Beef
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet or braiser over medium heat. Add the beef and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until browned.
Stir in the chopped onion, carrots, red pepper and garlic and the tomato paste. Season with the salt, pepper, smoked paprika and cumin and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring often.
Add the chopped cabbage, vinegar and water and stir well. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
If there's too much liquid, uncover and cook over medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes more. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Cajun spiced fish tacos
steps: Mix the Cajun seasoning and cayenne with a little salt and pepper on a large plate and coat the fish all over.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the fish over medium heat until golden. Lower the heat and cook for about 10 minutes in all, until cooked through. Cook it in batches if needed.
For the dressing, mix the sour cream with the lemon juice, the crushed garlic and a little salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas in the microwave for 5 to 10 seconds. Fill them with sliced avocado, shredded lettuce and green onions, a spoonful of salsa and large flakes of fish, and drizzle with the dressing.

title: Camaro Grelhado Com Molho Cru (Grilled Prawns with Green Onion Sauce)
steps: For the sauce, grind or blend the garlic, green onions, cumin, salt, vinegar and water into a paste.
Thread the shrimp onto skewers and brush them with some of the sauce.
Cook on a hot grill pan or barbecue for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until they are no longer see-through.
Serve with the rest of the sauce on the side.

title: Cambodian Stir-fried Morning Glory with Pork, Fermented Soybeans, and Garlic
steps: Cut the morning glory into 2-inch pieces and chop the garlic.
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a wok over medium heat and stir-fry the garlic for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the pork and break it up. Stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Stir in the fermented beans and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the morning glory and the sliced chili and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, so it stays bright green and crisp. Season with fish sauce and a pinch of sugar and serve right away with rice.

title: Carrot and Bean Fritters
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Drain the beans.
Grate the carrots and mash them with the beans, the flour and the crushed garlic. Season with thyme, chopped parsley, salt and pepper.
Shape the mixture into small patties and press each one into the breadcrumbs.
Fry the patties in hot oil for a few minutes on each side, until browned.
Move them to a lined baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.

title: Cassava pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Cut the chorizo into pieces and the pepper into strips.
Spread a little tomato sauce and mozzarella over each piece of cassava bread.
Top with the chorizo, ham, corn, olives and pepper.
Bake for 7 to 10 minutes and serve hot.

title: Cevapi Sausages
steps: Put the beef and pork in a bowl with the very finely chopped onion, grated garlic, parsley, paprika, baking powder, breadcrumbs, water, crumbled stock cube, salt and pepper.
Mix very well, cover and chill for 1 hour.
Shape portions of about 1/4 cup into rolls as thick as your thumb and 3 to 4 inches long. You should have about 18.
Cook them on a hot grill pan or barbecue for 12 to 14 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through. Serve hot.

title: Cheese Borek
steps: Whisk the egg with the chopped parsley, garlic and pepper flakes, then mix in the grated cheeses.
Lay one sheet of filo on a work surface, brush it with about 1 tbsp of the melted butter and cut it lengthwise into 4 strips.
Put a rounded teaspoon of filling at one end of each strip. Fold the corner over the filling to make a triangle and keep folding along the strip. Repeat with all the filo.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a large baking sheet. Lay the triangles on it in one layer.
Bake for about 30 minutes, until lightly browned, and serve warm.

title: Chicken & mushroom Hotpot
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Thinly slice the potatoes and boil them for 5 minutes, then drain. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes, then add the sliced mushrooms.
When they're almost cooked, stir in the flour and crumble in the stock cube. Stir over low heat for 2 minutes.
Take it off the heat and slowly stir in 2 cups (500 ml) of water. Season with pepper and a pinch each of nutmeg and mustard powder, then bring to a boil, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the cooked, diced chicken and the corn and pour everything into a buttered baking dish.
Lay the potato slices on top, slightly overlapping, brush them with a little melted butter and bake for about 35 minutes, until golden.

title: Chicken Alfredo Primavera
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the butter and 2 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper and cook for 5 to 7 minutes on each side, until cooked through. Let them rest on a board.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water for about 12 minutes, until al dente. Keep 1/2 cup of the pasta water and drain.

Lower the heat to medium and add the rest of the butter and oil to the skillet. Add the chopped squash, broccoli, mushrooms, bell pepper and onion and the pepper flakes, and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often, until tender.
Add the garlic with a pinch of salt and pepper for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it reduce by half, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the milk, cream and pasta water and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in the parmesan, the pasta and the sliced chicken. Season and serve with parsley.

title: Chicken and Potato Roti
steps: Melt 3 tbsp of sugar in a large saucepan over high heat until it caramelizes, then add the cubed chicken and stir until browned.
Add the chopped onions, garlic and parsley, the thyme, jerk seasoning, salt, pepper and the whole Scotch bonnet (don't cut it). Lower the heat and simmer for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, for the roti, sift the flour with a pinch of salt. Rub in the shortening, 1 tbsp at a time, until it looks like breadcrumbs. Mix in small amounts of water until you have a soft dough.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface into at least 12 very thin rounds and cover them with a towel.
Add 1 1/4 cups of water and the cubed potatoes to the chicken, cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes. Remove the Scotch bonnet.
Cook each roti on a hot, dry griddle for about 1 minute on each side, until browned but not crisp. To serve, spoon some filling onto each roti and fold it around.

title: Chicken Couscous
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the chopped onion for 1 to 2 minutes, until soft.
Add the diced chicken and fry for 7 to 10 minutes, until cooked through and the onion is golden. Grate in the ginger, stir in the harissa and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the apricots, drained chickpeas and couscous, pour in the broth and stir once.
Cover tightly and leave for about 5 minutes, until the couscous has soaked up the broth. Fluff it with a fork and scatter with cilantro. Serve with extra harissa if you like.

title: Chicken Enchilada Casserole
steps: Cut each chicken breast into 3 pieces and put them in a small pot with the enchilada sauce. Cover and cook over low to medium heat for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with two forks. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Spread about 1/4 cup of the sauce in a baking dish. Layer 2 tortillas, a third of the chicken, a third of the remaining sauce and a third of the cheese. Repeat twice.
Bake uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes, until bubbling and browned on top. Serve warm.

title: Chicken Fajita Mac and Cheese
steps: Fry the sliced onion and peppers and the garlic in the olive oil until soft.
Push the vegetables to the side and add the diced chicken. Add the fajita seasoning and salt and cook until the chicken colors slightly.
Add the cream, broth and macaroni and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the cheese until melted and serve topped with parsley.

title: Chicken Ham and Leek Pie
steps: Heat the broth in a saucepan, add the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.

Melt 2 tbsp (25 g) of the butter in a large heavy pan over low heat and cook the sliced leeks for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute. Add another 4 tbsp (50 g) of butter and, once it melts, stir in 3 tbsp of the flour for 30 seconds.
Slowly stir in the milk, a little at a time, then 1 cup (250 ml) of the broth and the wine, until smooth. Simmer for 3 minutes, season, stir in the cream and let it cool, covered.

Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) with a baking sheet inside. For the pastry, pulse the rest of the flour and butter in a food processor into fine crumbs, then add 1 beaten egg and the water until it forms a ball. Keep a third for the lid.
Roll out the rest about 1/4 inch thick and line a pie dish with it. Cut the chicken into 1-inch pieces and stir it into the sauce with the diced ham. Pour it into the dish.
Brush the rim with beaten egg, roll out the lid and press it on to seal. Cut a small hole in the middle, brush with egg and bake on the hot sheet for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden.

title: Chicken Handi
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot or wok and fry the sliced onions until deep golden brown. Lift them out and set them aside.
Fry the chopped garlic in the same pot for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomatoes and cook for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Return the onions and stir in the ginger paste. Add the cumin seeds, half of the coriander seeds and the chopped green chilies, then the turmeric and chili powder, and cook for a couple of minutes.
Add the chicken pieces, season with salt, cover and cook over medium-low heat for about 15 minutes, until almost cooked through. Don't rush this step.
When the oil separates from the spices, lower the heat as far as it goes and stir in the beaten yogurt so it doesn't split. Add the rest of the coriander seeds and half of the fenugreek.
Stir in the cream, sprinkle with the rest of the fenugreek and the garam masala, and serve hot with naan or roti.

title: Chicken Parmentier
steps: For the topping, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain, mash them well and stir in half of the butter, the cream and the egg yolks. Season.
For the filling, melt the rest of the butter in a large pan and gently fry the chopped shallots, carrots and celery until soft. Add the garlic.
Pour in the wine for 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes and broth and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until thickened. Add the cooked, shredded chicken, the olives and parsley and season.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Put the filling in an 8 x 12-inch baking dish, cover it with the mashed potato and grate the Gruyère over the top.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until piping hot and golden.

title: Chicken Quinoa Greek Salad
steps: Cook the quinoa as the package says, then rinse it in cold water and drain well.
Meanwhile, mash the butter with the chopped chili and garlic. Toss the chicken in 2 tsp of the oil with some salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in a hot grill pan for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until cooked through. Put it on a plate and dot it with the spicy butter to melt.
Mix the olives, sliced onion, crumbled feta and chopped mint in a bowl. Add the quinoa, the rest of the oil and the lemon juice and zest, and season well.
Serve with the chicken on top, drizzled with the buttery juices.

title: Chicken Salad With Mushrooms and Bacon
steps: Put the chicken in a saucepan, cover it with water, add 1 tsp of salt and simmer for about 15 minutes. Let it cool, then shred it with two forks.
Stir the mayonnaise, crème fraîche, mustard and vinegar together and season. Mix in the finely chopped shallot and the chicken.
Fry the bacon until crisp and drain it on paper towels.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in the same pan for about 5 minutes, until golden, and season.
Top the chicken salad with the bacon, mushrooms and chopped parsley, and serve on slices of bread.

title: Chicken Shawarma with homemade garlic herb yoghurt sauce
steps: Cut the chicken into small, thin slices and put them in a large zip-top bag.

Add 2 of the garlic cloves (crushed), the coriander, cumin, cardamom, cayenne, smoked paprika, salt, lemon juice and 2 tbsp of the oil. Close the bag, mix well and chill for 10 to 12 hours (or less if you're short on time).
Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in 2 batches, so the pan isn't crowded, for 5 to 8 minutes, until well browned and cooked through.
Meanwhile, mix the yogurt with the last garlic clove (crushed), a squeeze of lemon, a pinch of cumin and salt.
Serve the chicken in warm flatbreads with the garlic yogurt sauce, and lettuce, tomato and onion if you like.

title: Chicken wings with cumin, lemon & garlic
steps: Cut each wing in two at the joint with kitchen scissors.
Mix the crushed garlic, lemon zest and juice, cumin seeds and oil with plenty of salt and pepper. Toss the wings in it, cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight.

Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spread the wings on a baking sheet and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until crisp, drizzling the honey over them for the last 10 minutes. (On a barbecue, they take about 20 minutes.)
Serve with flatbreads, olives and plenty of napkins.

title: Chickpea Fajitas
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with foil. Drain the chickpeas, pat them dry and toss them on the sheet with the oil and paprika.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, shaking halfway, until browned and crisp.

Meanwhile, mix the chopped tomatoes and red onion with the vinegar and let them pickle. Mash the avocado with a fork, leaving some chunks, stir in the lime juice and season. Mix the sour cream with the harissa.
Heat a grill pan until very hot and char the tortillas on both sides, one at a time.
To build the fajitas, spread some harissa cream on each tortilla and top with chickpeas, avocado, the pickled salsa and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Chilean Empanada
steps: Hard-boil 4 of the eggs, then peel and chop them.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onion, garlic, oregano, cumin, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper for 5 to 7 minutes, until golden. Add the pork and cook for 7 to 10 minutes, until browned and crumbly.
Drain off the fat and stir in the raisins, sliced olives and chopped eggs. Set aside.
For the dough, mix the flour with the rest of the salt. Whisk the water with the melted shortening, pour it into the flour and mix into a dough. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet. Roll the dough out 1/8 inch thick and cut 12 circles. Spoon filling into the middle of each one, fold in half and seal with a fork.
Brush with the last egg, beaten, and bake for about 25 minutes, until golden brown.

title: Chorba Hamra bel Frik (Algerian Lamb, Tomato, and Freekeh Soup)
steps: Cover the freekeh with cold water and set it aside.
Put the diced lamb, chopped onion, pepper, paprika, cinnamon and salt in a pot. Stir in the oil, half of the chopped cilantro and mint, and the whole celery stalk. Cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir in the drained chickpeas, pour in just enough water to cover and bring back to a simmer. Add the diced zucchini and carrot and the tomato paste.
Grate the tomatoes into the soup, discarding the skins. Add the diced potato and enough water to cover, and simmer for about 10 minutes, until soft.
Drain the freekeh, add it to the soup and simmer for about 15 minutes, until tender. Remove the celery stalk and sprinkle with the rest of the cilantro and mint.

title: Choripán
steps: Cook the chorizos slowly on a grill or in a pan over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until cooked through. Cooking them slowly stops the skins from bursting.
Slice the bread rolls and toast them lightly.
Split each chorizo lengthwise, put it in a roll and top with plenty of chimichurri. Serve hot.

title: Chtitha Batata (Algerian Potato Stew)
steps: Grind the garlic, chili, cumin, paprika, black pepper, cayenne and salt into a paste with a mortar and pestle, then mix in the olive oil.
Fry the paste in a large saucepan over medium heat for 2 to 4 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, cut in half, and stir to coat them. Stir in the tomato paste and pour in just enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 40 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Serve the potatoes with the sauce spooned over.

title: Chuletas de Cerdo a la Criolla (Pork Chops in Creole Sauce)
steps: Put the pork chops in a zip-top bag with a spoonful of mustard, the cumin, crushed garlic, salt and pepper. Make sure they're coated and chill for 1 hour or overnight.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the chops for 3 minutes on each side. Set them aside on a warm plate.
Add the chopped onions and tomatoes to the pan, with a little more oil if needed. Cook over high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until softened.
Return the chops, cover and simmer over medium-low heat for about 15 minutes, until tender. Serve with the sauce spooned over and the cilantro on top.

title: Classic Potato Salad
steps: Boil the potatoes in lightly salted water for 10 to 12 minutes, until a fork slides out easily. Drain and let them cool.
Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and chop it into small pieces. If you prefer it less raw, soak it in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Finely chop the chives, red onion and radishes.
Stir the crème fraîche, mayonnaise, mustard, sugar and vinegar together and season.
Mix the potatoes and vegetables with the dressing, keeping some chives to sprinkle on top, season and serve.

title: Conch Fritters
steps: Grind or very finely chop the conch, the bell peppers, onions and chilies.
Mix in the lime juice, minced garlic, black pepper, salt, basil and pepper flakes, then the egg. Add the flour 1 tablespoon at a time, mixing until combined.
Cover and chill for 1 hour, or overnight for more flavor.
Heat about 2 inches of oil in a deep pan over medium-low heat. Drop in 1-inch balls of the mixture with two spoons and fry for 5 to 7 minutes, until golden and cooked inside.
Drain on paper towels and serve with tartar sauce and lime wedges.

title: Coq au vin
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pan and fry the chopped bacon until crisp. Drain it on paper towels. Fry the shallots in the pan for 5 to 8 minutes, until browned all over, and set them aside with the bacon.
Pat the chicken dry. Add the rest of the oil and brown the chicken in 2 batches, 5 to 8 minutes each, turning often. Set it aside.
Add the garlic briefly, then pour in the brandy over medium-high heat and scrape the bottom of the pan until most of it has bubbled away.

Return the legs and thighs, pour in the wine, broth and tomato paste, and add the thyme, rosemary and bay leaves tied together. Season, return the bacon and shallots, add the breasts, cover and simmer gently for 50 minutes to 1 hour.
Just before serving, fry the mushrooms in a non-stick pan over high heat until golden.

Move the chicken, bacon and shallots to a serving dish and remove the herbs. Mash the flour with the butter, bring the sauce to a gentle boil and whisk in small pieces of this paste. Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, then pour it over the chicken with the mushrooms and parsley.

title: Corba
steps: Rinse the lentils 2 or 3 times and drain them.
Heat a little olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook the chopped onion with a pinch of salt for about 3 minutes. Add the diced carrot and cook for 3 minutes more.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the cumin, paprika, mint, thyme, black pepper and pepper flakes and stir for 10 seconds.
Add the lentils, broth, water and salt and bring to a gentle boil. Lower the heat, half-cover and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
Blend until as smooth as you like, adjust the salt and serve with bread or crackers.

title: Corn on the cob with lime, green chilli and coconut butter
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a big, deep pan. Add the corn, cook for about 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and let it cool in the broth.
Drain the corn and char it in a very hot, dry frying pan for a couple of minutes on each side, two or three at a time.
Simmer the coconut milk with the lime juice and the chopped chili, season lightly, stir in the butter and set aside.
Toast the coconut in a hot, dry pan, stirring all the time, until golden. Let it cool, then mix it with the fried shallots and the chopped cilantro and parsley, and season.
Spoon the coconut milk mixture over each cob and sprinkle with the coconut mixture and lime zest.

title: Cottage Cheese And Feta Stuffed Peppers
steps: Cut the peppers in half lengthwise and remove the seeds.
Mix the feta, cottage cheese, chives, parsley, salt and lemon juice in a bowl.
Fill the peppers with the mixture, sprinkle with more chives and parsley, and serve.

title: Creamy Mustard Chicken
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season it with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken on all sides, about 10 minutes, turning a couple of times. Set it aside.
Cook the chopped onion and garlic for about 2 minutes, until soft. Add the broth, mustard, honey and cream and season.
Return the chicken, cover and cook over medium-low heat for about 45 minutes, until cooked through (170°F inside).
Serve over white rice with chopped parsley.

title: Creamy Tomato Soup
steps: Put the oil, chopped onions, celery, carrots and potatoes and the bay leaves in a big pot. Cook gently for 10 to 15 minutes, until the onions are soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, sugar, vinegar, canned tomatoes and tomato purée, and crumble in the stock cubes. Add 4 cups (1 liter) of boiling water and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Remove the bay leaves and blend until very smooth. Season, adding a pinch more sugar if needed.
To serve, reheat the soup and stir in the milk without letting it boil.

title: Crispy Eggplant
steps: Cut the eggplant into slices about 1/2 inch (1 cm) thick, sprinkle them with salt and let them sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse off the salt and pat the slices dry.
Mix the breadcrumbs and sesame seeds on a plate. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Dip each slice in egg, then in the crumbs, and fry for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.

title: Crispy fried fish with ginger and fermented soybeans (trey chien chuon)
steps: Cut the ginger into thin matchsticks and fry it in plenty of oil until golden and slightly crisp. Set it aside.
Cut the fish into strips, dust them very lightly with the tempura flour and fry them in the same oil until golden and crisp.
Drain the fermented soybeans in a colander. If they are very salty, rinse them first.

Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a deep pan and fry the chopped garlic until slightly golden. Add the soybeans and stir-fry for a few minutes, adding the sugar if they taste very salty. Add the water and cook for 1 minute.
Just before serving, stir in the fried ginger, the chopped green onions and the fish. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Crispy Sausages and Greens
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Strip the kale leaves from the stems and tear them into 1-inch pieces. Chop the cabbage.
Fry the sliced onion and mushrooms in a little olive oil until soft.
Put the greens in a large baking dish with the sliced garlic, onion and mushrooms. Coat with a little olive oil and pour the broth over.
Cover with foil and bake for about 15 minutes, until the greens wilt. Uncover, season and bake for 20 to 25 minutes more, until the cabbage is tender.

Meanwhile, prick the sausages and cook them in a little oil in a skillet over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Slice them and toss them with the greens, with a splash of vinegar if you like.

title: Crock Pot Chicken Baked Tacos
steps: Put the chicken in a pot with the dressing, cumin, smoked paprika and garlic. Cover and simmer over low heat for about 30 minutes, turning now and then, until cooked through. (In a slow cooker, cook on high for 4 hours.)
Lift out the chicken, shred it and mix it with most of the cooking liquid.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Stand the taco shells in a baking dish and fill each with a layer of refried beans, chicken and cheese.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese bubbles.
Meanwhile, blend the avocado with the green salsa until smooth, and thin the sour cream with the milk. Top the tacos with sliced tomatoes and jalapeño, then drizzle with both sauces.

title: Cuban Sandwich
steps: Put the pork chops in a baking dish, poke them all over with a fork, season with 1 tsp of salt and toss with the oil.
Mix the orange and lime zest and juice with the oregano, pepper and garlic powder. Pour half over the pork and let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Stir the mustard and mayonnaise into the rest of the marinade.
Roast the pork for 15 to 20 minutes, until it reaches 140°F inside, then slice it.
Cut the bread into 4 pieces, butter the outsides and spread the cut sides with the mustard sauce. Layer cheese, ham, pork, sliced pickles and more cheese, close the sandwiches and wrap each in foil.
Cook them in a heavy skillet over medium heat with another heavy pan on top as a press, 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until toasted and melted. Cut in half and serve.

title: Cucumber & fennel salad
steps: Slice the cucumber thinly and put it in a sieve. Sprinkle it with 1 tsp of salt and the sugar and leave it for 10 minutes.
Thinly slice the fennel and mix it with the drained cucumber.
Mix the sour cream with the lemon juice, vinegar and chopped dill, season with black pepper and stir it into the salad.

title: Curried Spinach from Botswana
steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the diced onion until lightly browned.
Add the curry powder and a little salt and toast for a few seconds.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the water and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the tomatoes break down.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook for 7 to 10 minutes more, until soft and wilted.

title: Dal fry
steps: Rinse the dal and soak it in about 3 cups of water for at least 1 hour, then drain it.
Cook the dal with 2 1/2 cups of water, the salt and the turmeric over medium-high heat for about 30 minutes, until soft and like a thick soup.
Heat the ghee in a frying pan and add the cumin and mustard seeds. When they crackle, add the bay leaves, chopped green chili, ginger and chili powder and stir for a few seconds.
Add the tomatoes and sugar and cook until the tomatoes are soft and mushy. Stir in the cilantro and garam masala for about 1 minute.
Pour this over the dal, mix well and cook for 1 minute more. Serve with naan or rice.

title: Easy Spanish chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Heat the oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium heat and fry the chopped onion, sliced chorizo and peppers with a pinch of salt and pepper for 15 minutes, until soft.
Add the paprika and garlic and cook for a few minutes, until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes, olives and drained butter beans and season. Nestle the chicken thighs in the sauce and season them well.
Bake for 40 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the chicken is cooked through. Scatter with parsley and serve.

title: Easy White Bean Soup
steps: Cover the beans with cold water and soak them for at least 4 hours or overnight. Drain and rinse.
Chop one onion and the carrots, and leave the other onion whole. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the chopped onion and carrots for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, water, whole peppers, whole onion, tomato paste, mint, thyme, savory, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer for about 2 hours, until the beans are tender.
Lift out the peppers and the whole onion. Mash the onion, peel and chop the peppers and return them to the pot.
Season to taste and serve with chopped parsley.

title: Escovitch Fish
steps: Rinse the fish, rub it with lime and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and fry the fish for 5 to 7 minutes on each side, until crisp and cooked through. Set it aside and pour off all but 2 to 3 tbsp of the oil.
Add the bay leaf, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for about 1 minute, without letting the garlic burn.
Add the sliced onion, peppers and carrot, the thyme, sliced Scotch bonnet, sugar, allspice and Worcestershire sauce and stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the vinegar, season and simmer for 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaf and thyme and spoon the sauce over the fish.

title: Falafel Pita Sandwich with Tahini Sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Bake the falafel on a baking sheet for 8 to 10 minutes, until hot.
Meanwhile, whisk the tahini, water, lemon juice, crushed garlic and paprika into a sauce.
Cut about 1 inch off the top of each pita to open a pocket.
Put 2 falafel in each pita with some lettuce, tomato, cucumber, pickle and red onion. Drizzle with about 1 tbsp of the tahini sauce and a little harissa.

title: Fårikål (Norwegian National Dish)
steps: Cut the lamb into large pieces and the cabbage into large wedges, keeping the core so they hold together.
Put a layer of lamb in the bottom of a large pot, fat side down, and sprinkle with some of the peppercorns, salt and flour. Add a layer of cabbage.
Repeat the layers, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Cover and cook over low heat for 2 to 3 hours, until the lamb falls off the bone.
Serve with boiled potatoes and plenty of the broth.

title: Fašírky
steps: Soak the bread in the milk until soft, then squeeze it out and crumble it.
Mix the pork with the finely chopped onion and garlic, the bread, 1 egg, the salt, pepper, marjoram, mustard and parsley.
Shape the mixture into palm-sized patties and flatten them slightly.
Dust each patty with flour, dip it in the other egg, beaten, and coat it with breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels and serve with mashed potatoes or salad.

title: Fasoliyyeh Bi Z-Zayt (Syrian Green Beans with Olive Oil)
steps: Put the green beans in a large pot, drizzle with the olive oil, season with salt and cover.
Cook over medium-high heat, stirring now and then, until done the way you like. In Syria they're cooked until they start to brown. They should steam in their own moisture, not fry.
Add the cilantro and the crushed garlic and cook just until the cilantro wilts. Serve warm with pita bread, or as a side dish.

title: Fennel Dauphinoise
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Thinly slice the potatoes and fennel, keeping the fronds, and crush the garlic.
Put them in a medium non-stick pan with the milk and cream, season well, cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring halfway, until the potatoes are just tender.
Divide the mixture between 2 small buttered ramekins and scatter with parmesan.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden and tender. Snip the fennel fronds over the top before serving.

title: Fettuccine Alfredo
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water as the package says, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the cream and butter in a large skillet over medium heat until the butter melts and the cream bubbles.
Whisk in the parmesan, season with salt and pepper and let the sauce thicken slightly.
Add the pasta and toss until coated. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Fish pie
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pan of cold salted water, bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 15 minutes, until tender. Drain, dry them over low heat for 30 seconds and mash with 1 tbsp of the oil. Season.

Meanwhile, put the milk and fish in a large pan and bring to a boil. Take it off the heat, cover and leave for 3 minutes. Lift out the fish, keeping the milk, and flake it into a baking dish without skin or bones.

Heat the rest of the oil in a pan, stir in the flour for 30 seconds, then gradually stir in about 1 cup (250 ml) of the milk. Grate in some nutmeg, season and let it bubble until thick. Stir in the cream.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grate the artichokes and add them to the dish with the sliced leek, the shrimp and the chopped herbs. Stir the lemon zest and juice into the sauce and pour it over.
Spoon the mash on top, rough it up with a fork, sprinkle with the cheese and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

title: Fish Soup (Ukha)
steps: Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat and cook the chopped onion, stirring now and then, until it starts to caramelize. Add the sliced carrots and cook for about 4 minutes more.
Add the stock, water, diced potatoes and bay leaves, season with salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Cover and cook over low heat for about 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Gently add the fish, cut into cubes, and bring back to a simmer. It cooks very fast: it's done when it's opaque and flakes easily.
Serve with chopped dill or parsley.

title: Fish Stew with Rouille
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp, keeping the tails on. Fry the shells in 1 tbsp of the oil for 5 minutes, until pink and golden. Add the wine and boil until reduced by two thirds, then add the stock. Strain and discard the shells.

Heat the rest of the oil in a deep frying pan, add the sliced fennel and onion and the garlic, season, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, boil the potato, cut into 3/4-inch chunks, for 5 minutes and drain.
Add a strip of orange zest, the star anise, the bay leaf and 1/2 tsp of the harissa to the pan and fry gently, uncovered, for 5 to 10 minutes, until soft and golden.

Stir in the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes and the shrimp stock and simmer for 10 minutes. Season. Scrub the mussels and remove the beards, throwing away any that stay open when tapped.

Gently stir in the potato, the fish in chunks and the shrimp. Bring back to a boil, cover and simmer for 3 minutes. Add the mussels, cover and cook for 2 minutes more, until they open (throw away any that stay closed).
Scatter with thyme leaves. For a quick rouille, stir the rest of the harissa into the mayonnaise. Serve in bowls with the rouille on top and bread on the side.

title: Fiskesuppe (Creamy Norwegian Fish Soup)
steps: Cut the fish into cubes, crush the garlic and cut the potatoes, carrots and leek into thin strips.
Heat the butter in a pot and add the garlic. When it starts to turn golden, whisk in the flour.
Add the fish stock, whisking until there are no lumps. Add the vegetables and milk, bring to a boil and cook for about 10 minutes.
Stir in the crème fraîche and bring back to a simmer. When it bubbles, turn off the heat, add the fish and let it cook in the hot soup for 5 minutes. Add the shrimp just before serving.
Sprinkle with chives and serve.

title: Flemish Hutsepot
steps: Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and cook the chopped onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped potatoes, bay leaves and thyme and cook for 5 minutes more.

Add the sliced carrots, diced turnips and sliced leek, the mustard and the broth, and season. Cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until everything is tender. Add a little water if needed.
Meanwhile, fry the sausages in a little oil until golden and cooked through.
When the potatoes start to fall apart, stir everything into a chunky stew and season to taste. Serve topped with the sausages and some extra mustard.

title: French Lentils With Garlic and Thyme
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, garlic, carrot and celery and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until soft.
Add 6 cups of water, the lentils, thyme, bay leaves and salt. Bring to a boil, then lower to a fast simmer.
Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils are tender and have absorbed most of the water. Drain any extra water and serve.

title: Frikadeller - Danish Meatballs
steps: Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Stir the salt into the pork, then mix in the flour, oats and pepper, the onion and garlic, the egg and lastly the milk. Stir until the mixture is firm, then chill it for at least 30 minutes.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Shape about 2 tablespoons of the mixture into each meatball with a spoon.
Fry them until well browned on both sides and cooked through. Serve hot with potato salad.

title: Ful Medames
steps: Soak the dried beans in cold water overnight, then drain them.
Cover them with fresh unsalted water in a large pan with a lid and simmer gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, until tender. Keep them covered with water, and add salt once they're soft.
Let the liquid reduce. Mash a ladle or two of the beans with some of the liquid and stir them back in to thicken.
Serve in bowls with chopped parsley. Let everyone add olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, cumin, salt and pepper to taste, and eat the beans lightly crushed with a fork, with flatbread.

title: Full English Breakfast
steps: Brush a griddle or large frying pan with a little oil and cook the sausages slowly over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, turning now and then, until golden. After 10 minutes, turn the heat up to medium.
Cut a few slits in the fat of the bacon and fry it for 2 to 4 minutes on each side.
Season the mushrooms, drizzle them with oil and cook stalk side up for 1 to 2 minutes, then turn and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more.

Cut the tomatoes in half, season and cook cut side down for 2 minutes, then turn and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. Slice the black pudding and cook it for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes on each side. Keep everything warm. Meanwhile, heat the baked beans in a small pan.
In a separate pan, fry the bread in oil for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until golden. Fry the eggs in the same pan, spooning the hot oil over them. Serve everything on warm plates.

title: Gallo pinto
steps: Heat a little oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion, bell pepper and cilantro, the cumin and salt, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the cooked beans, lower the heat to medium, add the Lizano sauce and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cooked rice and stir for 5 to 7 minutes, until it takes on all the flavors. Cook it less if you like it moist, longer if you like it toasted.

title: Gambas al ajillo
steps: Peel the shrimp, leaving the tails on, and remove the dark vein. Season with a little salt.
Put the sliced garlic, olive oil and chilies in a frying pan or terracotta dish over high heat.
When the garlic starts to turn golden, add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes on each side, until just pink.
Sprinkle with the parsley and some black pepper and serve right away.

title: Garides Saganaki
steps: Put the shrimp in a pot with enough water to cover and boil for 5 minutes. Drain and let them cool.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a saucepan and cook the chopped onion until soft. Add the chopped parsley, wine, tomatoes, garlic and the rest of the oil.
Simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Meanwhile, peel the shrimp, leaving the heads and tails on if you like.
Stir the shrimp into the sauce and simmer for about 5 minutes. Crumble in the feta, take it off the heat and let it stand until the cheese starts to melt. Serve warm with crusty bread.

title: General Tsos Chicken
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Whisk the flour, egg, 2 tbsp of the cornstarch, the baking powder, salt, onion salt, garlic powder and water into a smooth batter, and coat the chicken in it.
Heat oil for deep-frying to 350°F (175°C). Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden and crisp, and drain it on paper towels.
For the sauce, heat the sesame oil in a wok and fry the minced garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add the broth, duck sauce, soy sauce, honey, vinegar and gochujang and bring to a boil.
Mix the rest of the cornstarch with 2 tbsp of water and stir it in until the sauce thickens.
Toss the chicken in the sauce for 1 minute and serve sprinkled with the sliced green onions.

title: Gigantes Plaki
steps: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of water. Drain, rinse, cover with fresh water and simmer for about 50 minutes, until slightly tender but not soft. Drain.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the chopped onion and garlic over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft but not brown.
Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomatoes, sugar, oregano and a pinch of cinnamon and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes. Season well and stir in the beans.
Pour into a large baking dish and bake uncovered, without stirring, for about 1 hour, until the beans are tender and the sauce is thick.
Let it cool a little, then scatter with parsley and drizzle with olive oil.

title: Griddled aubergines with sesame dressing
steps: Slice the eggplants, brush the slices with oil and season.
Heat a grill pan until hot and cook the slices for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until golden and tender. Work in batches.
Mix the yogurt with the tahini, crushed garlic, lemon juice and most of the chopped herbs, and season.
Spoon the dressing over the eggplant and scatter with the rest of the herbs.

title: Grilled aubergines with spicy chickpeas & walnut sauce
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a pan and fry the chopped onion for about 10 minutes, until soft and lightly browned. Stir in the chopped chili, grated ginger and cumin.
Add the drained chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and 5 tbsp of water, bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Season and add the lemon juice.
Meanwhile, heat the broiler. Slice the eggplants lengthwise, brush them with oil, season and broil until golden. Turn them, brush again and broil until tender.
Mix the yogurt with the crushed garlic, most of the chopped walnuts and cilantro, and a little salt and pepper.
Arrange the eggplant on a warm plate, spoon the chickpeas over it, drizzle with the walnut sauce and scatter with the rest of the walnuts and cilantro.

title: Grilled corn with garlic mayo & grated cheese
steps: Boil the corn for 5 minutes and leave it in the water until you're ready to grill it.
Mix the crushed garlic with the mayonnaise.
Pat the corn dry, rub it with the garlic mayo and season.
Cook on a hot grill pan or barbecue for about 5 minutes, turning, until charred in places. Scatter with the parmesan and chopped cilantro and squeeze lime over the top.

title: Grilled eggplant with coconut milk
steps: Prick the eggplants all over with a fork so they don't burst.
Grill them over a gas flame or on a hot grill pan, turning often, until the skins are blackened and the flesh is soft.
Cool them in a bowl of water, peel off the skins and cut the flesh into bite-size pieces. Put them in a shallow dish.
Mix the coconut milk with the lemon juice, salt and pepper flakes, then taste and adjust. Pour it over the eggplant, sprinkle with sliced green onions and stir gently.

title: Grilled Mac and Cheese Sandwich
