steps: Cook the macaroni in well-salted boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes, until al dente, and drain. Mix the flour with the mustard powder, 1/2 tsp of the garlic powder, the salt, pepper and cayenne.

Melt 10 tbsp of the butter in the empty pan over low heat, whisk in the flour mixture and cook for about 1 minute, until nutty. Slowly whisk in the milk and cream and cook for about 2 minutes, until it starts to thicken.
Take it off the heat and stir in the grated Monterey Jack until melted, then the macaroni.
Spread it on a buttered, lined 9 x 13-inch baking sheet, cover with buttered parchment and chill for about 1 hour, until firm. Cut it into 8 pieces.
Mix the rest of the butter with the rest of the garlic powder and spread it on one side of each slice of bread.

Build each sandwich buttered side out: bread, a slice of cheddar, a piece of mac and cheese, a slice of Colby Jack, bread. Cook in a covered skillet over medium-low heat for about 4 minutes on each side, until browned and hot inside.

title: Grilled Portuguese sardines
steps: Mix the olive oil, crushed garlic, paprika, lemon juice, rosemary and chopped chili with some salt and pepper in a baking dish.
Add the sardines, toss well, cover and chill for a few hours.
Heat a grill pan or barbecue until hot and cook the sardines for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, until charred.
Drizzle with oil, sprinkle with a little more paprika and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Hodge Podge
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the diced potatoes and carrots for about 5 minutes, until just tender, then add the green beans and peas for 1 minute. Drain.
Melt the butter in a heavy pot over medium heat and warm the vegetables in it.
Add the milk and cream and bring to a boil, then lower the heat and season with the salt and pepper.
Add the dill and chives and simmer for at least 10 minutes. Serve warm.

title: Honey Balsamic Chicken with Crispy Broccoli & Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch wedges, toss them on one side of a baking sheet with a little oil, salt and pepper, and roast for 5 minutes.
Cut the broccoli into bite-size florets and chop the garlic. Warm the olive oil with half of the garlic in a small pan for 30 seconds.
Add the broccoli to the other side of the sheet, toss it with the garlic oil, salt and pepper, and roast for 15 to 20 minutes more, until browned and crisp.
Meanwhile, season the chicken and cook it in a little vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes on each side, until cooked through. Set it aside.
In the same pan, cook the rest of the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the vinegar, honey and broth and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until thick and glossy. Take it off the heat and stir in the butter.
Turn the chicken in the glaze and serve with the potatoes and broccoli.

title: Honey Teriyaki Salmon
steps: Whisk the soy sauce and sake together and coat the salmon in it.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the salmon on both sides, adding the rest of the glaze, until it's cooked through and the glaze has thickened.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve right away.

title: Imam bayildi with BBQ lamb & tzatziki
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Halve the eggplants lengthwise, score the flesh deeply, brush with plenty of olive oil and roast on a baking sheet for about 20 minutes, until soft.
Fry the chopped onion in a little oil until soft, then add the garlic and cinnamon for 1 minute.

Scoop out the middle of the eggplants, chop it and add it to the onions. Halve the tomatoes, scoop the seeds and juice into a sieve over a bowl, chop the flesh and add it to the pan. Cook for 10 minutes, until soft, and stir in most of the parsley.
Lay the eggplant halves in a baking dish, fill them with the tomato mixture, pour over the tomato juice, drizzle with oil and bake for 30 minutes.
For the tzatziki, mix the yogurt with the grated cucumber and chopped mint and season.

Season the lamb with salt, pepper and a pinch of paprika and cook on a hot grill pan for 3 minutes on each side. Squeeze lemon over it and serve with the eggplant, the rest of the parsley and the tzatziki.

title: Irish stew
steps: Soak the wheat berries overnight. Drain, cover with plenty of water and simmer for about 1 hour, until cooked. Drain.

Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Season the lamb with 1 tsp of salt and some pepper. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large, deep pan with a lid and brown the lamb in batches, about 4 minutes on all sides. Set it aside.

Lower the heat to medium and fry the shallots in a little more oil for about 4 minutes, until caramelized. Then brown the carrots, turnips, celeriac and potatoes, cut into chunks, in batches, adding oil as needed.
Pour the wine into the pan with the sugar, herbs, 1 tsp of salt and plenty of pepper and boil for about 3 minutes.

Return the lamb, vegetables and wheat berries, add the broth, cover and boil for 5 minutes, then cook in the oven for 1 1/2 hours. If there's a lot of liquid, boil it uncovered for a few minutes before serving.

title: Jamaican Beef Patties
steps: For the pastry, mix the flour with 1 tsp of the salt and the curry powder. Rub in the butter until it's in small pieces coated with flour.
Mix in about 1/2 cup of ice water, then 2 to 3 tbsp at a time until it forms a dough. Cut it into 12 pieces, cover and chill for 30 minutes.

For the filling, mix the beef with the allspice and black pepper. Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the chopped onion until translucent, then the chopped Scotch bonnet, garlic and thyme for 1 minute, with the rest of the salt.

Add the beef and cook until no longer pink, breaking up any clumps. Stir in the ketchup and about 2 cups of water, bring to a boil and simmer until the liquid has reduced to a thick sauce. Let it cool completely.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Roll each piece of dough into a 5-inch circle, put 3 heaped tablespoons of filling on one half, wet the edges, fold over and crimp with a fork.
Beat the egg with a splash of water, brush it over the patties and bake on lined sheets for about 30 minutes, until golden.

title: Jamaican Curry Goat
steps: Rinse the goat meat. Mix it with 1 1/2 tbsp of the curry powder, the all-purpose seasoning, ground ginger, allspice, sliced onion, garlic and thyme. Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Pick out the onion and garlic and set them aside. Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the goat for 2 to 3 minutes on each side. Set it aside.
Add a little more oil and the rest of the curry powder for 10 seconds, then the onion and garlic for about 4 minutes, until soft, adding a little water if dry.
Return the goat with the water, cover and simmer over low heat for about 2 hours, until tender, adding water as needed. (In a pressure cooker, cook for 40 minutes on high.)
Add the cubed potato and the whole Scotch bonnet and cook for 15 minutes more, until the potato is soft. Remove the pepper, season and serve with rice.

title: Jamaican Pepper Shrimp
steps: Mix the shrimp with the minced Scotch bonnets, the all-purpose seasoning, annatto and allspice, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Bring the shrimp stock to a gentle simmer in a large pan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and garlic and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add the shrimp and thyme, cover and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until the shrimp are bright orange and cooked through.
Stir in the vinegar for 1 minute and add salt to taste. Serve hot with some of the cooking liquid.

title: Jamaican Rice and Peas
steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, drained kidney beans, water, salt, allspice and pepper in a large pot and stir. Lay the green onions, thyme and whole Scotch bonnet on top.
Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat for 18 minutes.
Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes more.
Remove the green onions, Scotch bonnet and thyme, fluff with a fork and serve.

title: Jamaican Steamed Cabbage
steps: Shred the cabbage and slice the carrots, tomato, onion, garlic, green onions and Scotch bonnet.
Put everything in a large pan with the thyme, water, oil, butter, salt and pepper and cover.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, then lower the heat and cook for 5 minutes more, until the cabbage is tender. Remove the thyme stalks and serve.

title: Jamon & wild garlic croquetas
steps: Wash the wild garlic, pour boiling water over it until just wilted, rinse it under cold water, squeeze it dry and chop finely.

Warm the milk in a pan until steaming. In a second pan, warm the olive oil and stir in the flour for a couple of minutes, until lightly browned. Gradually add the milk until you have a thick, smooth sauce, and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes. Season.
Beat in the grated manchego, chopped ham and wild garlic. Spread it on an oiled plate, cover and chill for at least 1 hour.
With oiled hands, shape it into 18 to 20 balls and freeze them for 30 minutes to firm up.
Dip each ball in the beaten egg, then roll it in the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pan, no more than a third full, to 340°F (170°C). Fry the croquetas in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until deep golden, and drain on paper towels. Serve warm.

title: Jerk chicken with rice & peas
steps: For the jerk marinade, blend the juice of 1 lime, the green onions, ginger, garlic, onion, chilies, dried thyme, soy sauce, oil, brown sugar, allspice and 1 tsp of salt into a thick paste. Don't add water. Taste and add more chili or sugar if needed.
Cut a few slashes in the chicken, rub the marinade in well, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.

Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Roast the chicken in a roasting pan with the squeezed lime halves for about 45 minutes, until cooked through. (On a barbecue, cook it slowly over indirect heat for about 30 minutes.)

Meanwhile, rinse the rice and put it in a large saucepan with the coconut milk, thyme sprigs, a pinch of salt and 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) of cold water. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Stir in the drained beans, cover and leave off the heat for 5 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed. Squeeze the roasted lime over the chicken and serve with the rice and peas.

title: Kadu Borani
steps: Peel the squash and cut it into 1/2-inch (1 cm) slices. Deep-fry them in oil until golden and set aside.
Deep-fry the sliced onions in the same oil until golden, then grind them with the garlic into a paste.
Heat a little oil in a pan over medium heat and add the turmeric. Dissolve the salt in 1 cup of the water and add it. Layer the squash and the onion paste in the pan until both are used up.
Add the sugar and the rest of the water, lower the heat and cook until the water has reduced.
Spread some yogurt on a plate, put the squash on top, cover with more yogurt and finish with sliced green chili.

title: Kafteji
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2-inch cubes. Heat about 1/2 inch of olive oil in a large pan until very hot and fry them for about 20 minutes, turning now and then, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Meanwhile, rub the halved, seeded pepper with oil and broil it cut side down until the skin is blackened. Put it in a sealed bag for 15 minutes, then peel it.
In another pan, fry the onions, sliced into thin rings, in more oil for about 15 minutes, until golden, and add the ras el hanout at the end.
Cut the pumpkin into 2-inch cubes and fry it in the potato pan for 10 to 15 minutes, until soft and browned. Drain.
Pour off the oil, put all the vegetables back in the pan and mix. Pour the beaten eggs over them, cover and cook until set.
Tip everything onto a large board, season and chop it all together with a big knife.

title: Kapsalon
steps: Bake the fries until golden, as the package says, and spread them over a baking dish.
Cut the doner meat into strips and fry them in a little oil for about 6 minutes.
Spread the meat over the fries and cover with the cheese. Put it in the oven for a few minutes, until the cheese melts.
Chop the lettuce, tomato and cucumber into a simple salad and spread it over the top. Serve with garlic sauce and hot sauce.

title: Karbonader (Lean Beef Patties) with Caramelized Onions
steps: Grate half an onion and slice the rest. Fry the sliced onions in 2 tbsp of the butter over low to medium heat until caramelized.
Mix the beef with the grated onion, salt, pepper, nutmeg, cornstarch and water.
Shape it into a log and cut it into 6 patties. Mark a light crisscross pattern on each with a knife.
Brown the patties on both sides in the rest of the butter over high heat, then lower the heat and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more.
Serve with the onions and boiled potatoes.

title: Kaspressknödel - Cheese Dumplings
steps: Mix the cubed bread with the milk and a pinch of salt and let it soak for a while.
Add the grated potatoes, grated cheese, eggs and chopped parsley.
Fry the diced onion in a little butter until golden and add it to the mixture.
Add the flour and knead gently. Shape into round dumplings and press them flat.
Fry them in butter on both sides until golden brown. Serve in a clear broth or with a salad.

title: Katsu Chicken curry
steps: For the sauce, heat a little of the oil in a medium non-stick saucepan and cook the chopped onions and garlic until soft. Add the chopped carrots and cook over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in 1 tbsp of the flour and the curry powder for 1 minute. Gradually stir in the broth, then add the honey, soy sauce and bay leaf and slowly bring to a boil.
Simmer for about 20 minutes, until thickened but still pourable. Stir in the garam masala, strain the sauce and keep it warm.
Season the chicken. Coat each breast in the rest of the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Slice the chicken, pour the curry sauce over it and serve with white rice.

title: Kedgeree
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan with a lid and gently fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes, until soft but not colored. Add the coriander and curry powder, season with salt and fry for about 3 minutes, until fragrant.

Stir in the rice, add 2 1/2 cups (600 ml) of water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 to 15 minutes more, without lifting the lid.
Meanwhile, put the haddock and bay leaves in a frying pan, cover with the milk and poach for 10 minutes, until the fish flakes. Remove the skin and break the fish into large flakes.
Boil the eggs for 4 1/2 to 5 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel them and cut them into quarters.
Gently mix the fish, eggs, chopped parsley and cilantro into the rice and serve hot, with a few extra herbs on top.

title: Kelem dolmasi
steps: Boil the rice for 8 minutes and drain. Finely chop the onion and herbs, and roughly mash the drained chickpeas.
Mix the lamb with the minced lamb fat, onion, turmeric, cinnamon, chickpeas, rice and herbs, and season well with salt and pepper.

Bring a very large pot of salted water to a boil. Pull off the outer cabbage leaves and keep them. Boil the rest of the cabbage whole for 3 to 4 minutes, then peel off the softened leaves. Repeat until you have all the leaves you can use.
Cut out the tough stalks and halve the largest leaves. Put a heaped tablespoon of filling on each leaf, fold in the ends and roll it up tightly.

Line the bottom of a large pot with the outer leaves and stalks and lay the rolls on top. Add water up to the top of the lining leaves, weigh the rolls down with a heatproof plate and simmer for 25 minutes.
Heat the tomato paste with the water for a few minutes, pour it over the rolls and cook for 5 minutes more.

title: Kenyan Beef Curry
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a large pot. Add the cubed beef, crushed garlic and ginger, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring now and then. Drain, keeping the cooking water.
Heat the oil in the same pot over medium heat and cook the chopped onions for 5 to 7 minutes, until soft. Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until falling apart.
Add the beef and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then. Stir in the paprika, pepper, curry powder, tomato paste and salt to taste.

Pour back the cooking water, with extra water to cover. Bring to a boil and simmer uncovered for about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the meat is tender and the sauce thick. Add water if it starts to stick.
Taste, adjust the seasoning and garnish with sliced chili and cilantro.

title: Keto Banitsa
steps: Heat the oven to 360°F (180°C) and butter an 8 x 8-inch baking dish.
Beat the eggs in a bowl, then slowly whisk in the melted butter.
Stir in the grated mozzarella, crumbled feta and cream cheese, then whisk in the baking powder.
Pour it into the dish, sprinkle with sesame seeds if you like and bake for about 20 minutes, until golden.
Let it cool in the dish for 5 to 10 minutes, then cut it into pieces.

title: Kidney Bean Curry
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over low-medium heat. Cook the chopped onion with a pinch of salt, stirring now and then, until soft and starting to color.
Add the garlic, grated ginger and chopped cilantro stalks and cook for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Add the cumin, paprika and garam masala for 1 minute more.
Tip in the tomatoes and the kidney beans with their liquid and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Season the curry and serve with the rice and the cilantro leaves.

title: Koshari
steps: Rinse the rice and soak it in water while you cook the lentils. Boil the lentils in 4 cups of water, then simmer for 15 to 17 minutes, until just tender but still firm. Drain and season with a little salt.
Drain the rice and cook it with the lentils, 1 tbsp of the oil, salt, pepper and the coriander over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, stirring.
Add warm water to cover by about 1 1/2 inches (about 3 cups), bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat for about 20 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed. Leave covered for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente and drain. Warm the drained chickpeas.
Fry the onion, sliced into thin rings and salted, in the rest of the oil over medium-high heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and crisp.
Serve the rice and lentils topped with the pasta, chickpeas and crispy onions.

title: Kumpir
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Prick the potatoes and bake them for about 1 1/2 hours, until the skins are crisp and the inside is very soft.
Meanwhile, grate the cheese and finely chop the onion and red pepper.
Split each potato open and mash the butter into the flesh with a fork, then mix in most of the cheese.
Top with the onion, pepper, the rest of the cheese, salt, pepper and some pepper flakes if you like. Add any other toppings you enjoy, such as corn or olives.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
steps: Mix the sake, soy sauce and sesame oil with the cornstarch dissolved in the water, and divide it in half.
Toss the chicken, cut into pieces, with half of the mixture, cover and chill for about 30 minutes.

In a frying pan, mix the other half with the chili powder, vinegar and sugar, then add the chopped green onions and garlic, the water chestnuts and the peanuts. Heat slowly over medium heat until fragrant.
Meanwhile, cook the chicken in a little oil in a large frying pan until cooked through.
Add the chicken to the sauce and simmer together until the sauce thickens. Serve with rice.

title: Kung Po Prawns
steps: Mix the cornstarch with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, toss in the shrimp and set aside for 10 minutes. Stir the rest of the soy sauce, the tomato paste, both sugars and 2 tbsp of water together into a sauce.
Heat a large frying pan or wok until very hot, add the oil and fry the shrimp until golden in places. Tip them out.
Add the peanuts, sliced chilies and sliced water chestnuts and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the peanuts start to color. Add the grated ginger and garlic for 1 minute more.
Return the shrimp, pour in the sauce and simmer for 2 minutes, until slightly thick. Serve with rice.

title: Lakra me Mish Cabbage and Meat Stew
steps: Heat some olive oil in a large pan with a lid. Add the chopped onion, diced beef and sliced peppers and fry for 5 minutes, stirring, until the meat is browned.
Add the paprika, tomato paste and pepper flakes, season and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the chopped cabbage and fry for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Pour in the boiling water so it covers the cabbage by about 1 inch, cover and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 2 1/2 hours, until the cabbage is soft and the meat tender. Let it cool for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Lakror me Kungull Summer Squash Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Grate the squash and mix it with the eggs and baking powder.
Add the flour and mix to a thick, sticky batter, adding a little more flour if it's runny.
Rub a deep round baking pan with olive oil and spread the batter in it. Rub a little oil over the top with your hand to smooth it.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until golden brown. Let it cool before cutting into squares.

title: Laksa King Prawn Noodles
steps: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan and cook the sliced chili for 1 minute. Add the curry paste and cook for 1 minute more.
Dissolve the stock cube in 3 cups (700 ml) of boiling water, pour it into the pan, add the coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add the fish sauce and a little seasoning, then the noodles, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft.
Squeeze in the juice of 1 lime, add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot through.
Serve in bowls with the cilantro and the other lime cut into wedges.

title: Lamb and Potato pie
steps: Dice the lamb and dust it lightly with the flour.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a large saucepan and fry the chopped onion and lamb until lightly browned. Season.
Add the sliced carrots and the broth, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for at least 1 hour, until the meat is tender.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Boil the cubed potatoes until just tender, drain and add them to the lamb.
Pour into a pie dish, cover with the pastry and cut three slits in the top. Brush with beaten egg and bake for about 40 minutes, until golden.

title: Lamb Biryani
steps: Grind half of the cashews with the poppy seeds and cumin seeds into a smooth paste, using as little water as possible.
Deep-fry the sliced onions until light brown and drain them on paper towels. Fry the rest of the cashews until golden. Rinse the rice and soak it for 20 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a large, wide pan over medium heat. Fry the cashew paste, ginger-garlic paste, chopped garlic, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and bay leaf for 1 minute.
Stir in the chili powder, biryani masala and half of the chopped mint and cilantro. Take it off the heat, stir in the yogurt, then return it to the heat.
Add the lamb, salt and 1/2 cup of water. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for about 1 hour, until tender. Uncover to dry off any extra liquid.

Boil the drained rice in plenty of salted water for 7 minutes, until 80% cooked, and drain. Spread it over the lamb and top with the fried onions and cashews, the rest of the herbs and the saffron soaked in a spoonful of warm water.
Cover tightly and cook over medium heat for 12 minutes, then over the lowest heat for 5 minutes. Mix gently and serve hot.

title: Lamb Pilaf (Plov)
steps: Cover the prunes with water, add the lemon juice and soak for at least 1 hour. Drain and chop them.
Meanwhile, heat the butter in a large pan and cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the cubed lamb and crushed garlic and fry for 5 minutes, stirring, until browned.
Pour in 2/3 cup (150 ml) of the broth, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour, until the lamb is tender.
Add the rest of the broth and bring to a boil. Stir in the rinsed rice and a large pinch of saffron, cover and simmer for about 15 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Stir in the prunes, season and heat through for a few minutes. Serve on a warm dish with parsley.

title: Lamb Tagine
steps: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pan and cook the chopped onion and carrots for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the diced lamb and brown it all over. Stir in the garlic, grated ginger, cumin, saffron and cinnamon and cook for a few minutes, until fragrant.
Add the honey and apricots, crumble in the stock cube and pour in about 2 cups (500 ml) of boiling water, enough to cover the meat. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Uncover and cook for 30 minutes more, then stir in the cubed squash. Cook for 20 to 30 minutes, until the squash is soft and the lamb tender.
Serve with couscous and chopped parsley.

title: Lamb tomato and sweet spices
steps: Drain the vine leaves, soak them in boiling water for 10 minutes and dry them on a towel.

For the filling, mix the lamb with the chopped onion, grated potato, rice, parsley, cilantro, cloves and cinnamon. Halve 2 of the tomatoes, grate them into the bowl and throw away the skins. Add 1/2 tsp of salt and some pepper, then squeeze out any juice.

For the sauce, heat the oil in a medium pan and cook the grated ginger and crushed garlic for 1 to 2 minutes. Grate in the rest of the tomatoes, add the lemon juice and sugar, season and simmer for 20 minutes.
Line a wide, heavy pan with any torn leaves and cover the bottom with the fennel, cut into 1/4-inch slices.
Put 2 teaspoons of filling at the base of each leaf, fold in the sides and roll it up tightly. Pack the rolls seam side down in the pan.

Pour the sauce over them, adding water just to cover. Weigh them down with a plate, cover, bring to a boil and simmer very gently for 70 minutes, until most of the liquid has gone. Serve warm with rice.

title: Lao Naem Khao
steps: Thinly slice the onion and shallot and soak them in ice water while you cook.
Mix the cooked rice with the grated coconut using your hands, and roll it into 2-inch balls.
Heat oil for deep-frying. Dip each ball in the beaten eggs and fry until deep golden and crunchy. Drain on paper towels and let them cool.

Break the rice balls into pieces in a large bowl. Add the drained onion and shallot, the sausage torn into small pieces, the chopped pickled garlic, the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, sliced green onions, cilantro and mint, and mix.
Top with the peanuts and serve with lettuce leaves and fresh vegetables.

title: Lasagna Sandwiches
steps: Mix the sour cream, finely chopped onion, oregano and salt, and spread it on 4 slices of bread.
Cook the bacon until crisp.
Layer the bacon, tomato and cheese on the bread and top with the other slices.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet and toast the sandwiches on both sides until browned and the cheese melts, adding more butter if needed.

title: Leblebi Soup
steps: Soak the dried chickpeas overnight and drain them.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the chopped onion until translucent. Add the chickpeas and broth, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Toast the cumin in a dry pan, then pound it with the garlic and salt into a fine paste.
Stir the paste and harissa into the soup and simmer for about 30 minutes more, until the chickpeas are tender.
Season with pepper and lime juice and serve hot.

title: Leg of Lamb Armenian-Style
steps: Put the lamb in a roasting pan with the crushed garlic, chopped parsley, onion and mint, the pepper, vinegar, olive oil and salt. Turn it to coat.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for 2 days, turning it now and then.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and roast for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until cooked the way you like. Let it rest before slicing.

title: Ma Po Tofu
steps: Mix the beef with a pinch of salt and the sesame oil. Mix the cornstarch with 2 1/2 tbsp of water.
Cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes. Simmer them in salted boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the beef until crisp. Lift it out, leaving the oil.
Fry the doubanjiang over low heat for 1 minute, then add the chopped garlic, the white parts of the green onions, the ginger and the fermented black beans for 30 seconds. Stir in the pepper flakes.
Add the water and bring to a boil. Slide in the tofu, add the soy sauce and beef and simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture in two parts, 30 seconds apart, until the sauce coats the tofu. Sprinkle with ground Sichuan pepper and the green parts of the onions and serve with rice.

title: Macaroni Pie
steps: Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water for about 8 minutes, until tender. Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Drain the macaroni, return it to the hot pan and mix in the butter, then most of the grated cheese.
Whisk the egg until fluffy and add the milk, onion powder, mustard, black pepper, salt and cayenne. Mix it into the macaroni.
Pour into a greased baking dish and top with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 30 to 45 minutes, depending on the depth of the dish, until set and golden.

title: Massaman Beef curry
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and roast the peanuts on a baking sheet for 5 minutes, until golden. Chop them roughly. Lower the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Heat 2 tbsp of the coconut cream in a large casserole with a lid. Fry the curry paste for 1 minute, then stir in the cubed beef until coated.
Add the rest of the coconut cream with 3/4 cup of water, the cubed potatoes, the chopped onion, lime leaves, cinnamon, tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and most of the peanuts.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Sprinkle with the sliced chili and the rest of the peanuts and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Mastawa Lamb and Rice
steps: Put the lamb, cut into pieces, in a large pan with the chopped onions and the turmeric, and add water to cover. Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for about 1 1/2 hours, until the meat comes off the bones easily.
Meanwhile, cut the orange peel into thin matchsticks, removing as much white pith as you can, and soak it in a bowl of water.
Lift out the meat, pull it off the bones in strips and return it to the pan.

Rinse the rice and add it with salt to taste. The liquid should cover the rice by about 3/4 inch, so add water if needed. Bring back to a boil and cook uncovered over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the rice is al dente and the liquid absorbed.
Carefully stir in the yogurt. Fry the crushed garlic in the oil and add it with the dill, pepper, drained chickpeas and drained orange peel. Season.
Cover the pan with a clean towel and the lid and leave on low heat for about 30 minutes. Serve with warm naan.

title: Matar Paneer
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat. Add the cubed paneer, lower the heat a little and brown it on all sides. It browns quickly, so don't walk away. Drain it on paper towels.
Fry the grated ginger, cumin, turmeric, coriander and chopped chili in the pan for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, mash them with a spoon and simmer for 5 minutes, adding a splash of water if it's too thick. Season well.
Add the peas and simmer for 2 minutes, then stir in the paneer and sprinkle with the garam masala. Top with cilantro and serve with naan, roti or rice.

title: Mbuzi Choma (Roasted Goat)
steps: Season the goat meat with salt and roast it over a medium charcoal fire for about 50 minutes, turning and salting it as you go. Without a grill, roast it in a 375°F (190°C) oven.
For the ugali, bring about 4 cups of water with a pinch of salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan. Slowly pour in the cornmeal, stirring.
Lower the heat to medium-low and keep stirring, pressing out any lumps, for about 10 minutes, until very thick and pulling away from the pan. Shape it into a ball with wet hands.
For the kachumbari, mix the chopped tomatoes, onion, chili and cilantro. Serve the goat with the ugali and the salad.

title: Meang Nem
steps: Rinse the rice, soak it for 10 minutes and drain well. Toast it in a dry wok over medium heat, stirring all the time, for about 5 minutes, until dark golden. Let it cool, then grind it finely and sift it.

Thinly slice the shallots and finely chop the galangal, pickled scallions, chilies and orange zest. Roast and coarsely grind the peanuts. Toast the coconut in a dry pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir the lime juice, orange juice, palm sugar, pickling brine and fish sauce together until the sugar dissolves.
Mix the dried shrimp, toasted coconut, chopped aromatics and dressing, then stir in the rice powder. Top with the peanuts.
Serve on a large plate and let everyone wrap a little in lettuce leaves with fresh vegetables.

title: Mediterranean Pasta Salad
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pan of salted boiling water for about 10 minutes, or as the package says.
Meanwhile, quarter the tomatoes and slice the olives. Put the tomatoes in a salad bowl, tear the basil over them and mix with 1 tbsp of the oil.
Drain the pasta and cool it under cold running water.
Toss it with the tomatoes, then add the olives, the drained mozzarella and the tuna in chunks. Mix and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Just before serving, add plenty of black pepper and drizzle with the rest of the oil.

title: Mee goreng mamak
steps: Fry the peanuts, dried chilies and dried shrimp in 1 tbsp of the oil over medium heat until fragrant. Blend them with the tamarind paste and the water until fine.
Cook this paste in 2 tbsp of the oil over low heat until the oil separates and it turns darker.

Boil the potatoes, cut into small chunks, until tender, and drain. Slice the onions and tofu, mince the garlic and cut up the cabbage and Chinese broccoli. If the noodles are dried, boil them to soften. Mix the soy sauce with a splash of water.
Cook one portion at a time: heat a little oil in a wok and add a quarter of the garlic, onion and paste. Cook until fragrant, then add a quarter of the tofu, potatoes and greens for 30 seconds.
Add a quarter of the noodles and 3 tbsp of the soy mixture and toss for 1 minute. Push the noodles aside, scramble in a quarter of the egg, then mix. Repeat for the other portions.

title: Montreal Smoked Meat
steps: For the cure, mix the salt with 3 tbsp of the pepper, 1 tbsp of the coriander, the sugar, bay leaf and cloves. Rub it all over the brisket, put it in a large zip-top bag and cure it in the coldest part of the fridge for 4 days, turning it twice a day.
Rinse off as much of the cure as you can and soak the brisket in cold water for 2 hours, changing the water every 30 minutes. Pat it dry.
For the rub, mix the rest of the pepper and coriander with the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, dill, mustard, celery salt and pepper flakes. Coat the brisket all over.
Smoke it at 225°F (110°C), fat side up, for about 6 hours, until it reaches 165°F inside. Without a smoker, cook it on a rack in a 225°F oven.
Put the brisket on a rack in a roasting pan with 1 inch of water, cover with foil and steam it over two burners on medium heat for 1 to 2 hours, until it reaches 180°F, adding hot water as needed.
Let it cool slightly, then slice it and serve on rye bread with mustard.

title: Moroccan Carrot Soup
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Toss the chopped carrots, onion and garlic with the cumin, coriander, a pinch of salt and the oil, and spread them on a baking sheet.
Roast for 10 to 12 minutes, until the carrots soften. Let them cool.
Blend with a little water into a smooth purée and strain it into a pan.
Add 2 cups of water, bring to a boil and stir in the garam masala and salt to taste.
Take it off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and serve hot.

title: Moussaka
steps: Heat the broiler to high. Brown the beef in a deep ovenproof frying pan over high heat for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, prick the eggplant with a fork and microwave it on high for 3 to 5 minutes, until soft. Mix the yogurt, egg and parmesan and season.
Stir the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste and diced cooked potatoes into the beef, season and heat through. Smooth the top.
Slice the eggplant and lay it on top, pour the yogurt mixture over it and spread it evenly.
Broil until the topping has set and turned golden.

title: Mulukhiyah
steps: Cook the chopped onion in 3 to 4 tbsp of the olive oil until soft.
Add the cubed beef and sear it for 3 to 4 minutes on each side.
Pour in the water, or just enough to cover, and cook over medium heat for about 45 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Add the frozen mulukhiyah and stir until it thaws and comes to a boil.

In another pan, warm the rest of the oil with the crushed garlic over medium-low heat until fragrant, without browning it. Stir it into the soup and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes. Add the salt and serve with lemon juice and rice or pita.

title: Mushroom & Chestnut Rotolo
steps: Soak the dried mushrooms in 1 1/2 cups (350 ml) of boiling water. Blend three quarters of the chestnuts with 2/3 cup (150 ml) of water until creamy, and chop the rest.

Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan and fry the chopped shallots with a pinch of salt until soft. Add the garlic, chopped chestnuts and rosemary for 2 minutes, then the wild mushrooms with 2 more tbsp of oil, and cook for 3 minutes.
Drain and chop the soaked mushrooms, keeping the liquid, and add them with the soy sauce for 2 minutes more.
Whisk the wine, mushroom liquid and chestnut cream into a sauce and season. Add half of it to the pan and cook for 1 minute, until glossy. Remove the rosemary.

Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Cook the lasagne sheets in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, then plunge them into ice water and lay them on a towel. Spread the mushroom mixture over each, roll them up from the short end and cut each roll in half.

Stand the rolls cut side up in a baking dish, pour the rest of the sauce over and bake for 10 minutes. Toss the breadcrumbs with 2 tbsp of oil and the sage, scatter them over and bake for 10 minutes more, until golden. Drizzle with truffle oil if you like.

title: Mushroom soup with buckwheat
steps: Chop the onion and garlic, slice the mushrooms and rinse the buckwheat.
Heat the oil and lightly fry the onion, then add the mushrooms and garlic and keep frying.
Add salt, the stock cube, the buckwheat and the bay leaf, cover with water and simmer gently for about 20 minutes.
Just before it's done, stir in the sour cream mixed with the flour, pepper, chopped parsley and vinegar to taste.

title: Mustard champ
steps: Boil the potatoes for about 15 minutes, until tender. Drain and mash them.
Heat the milk and half of the butter in a corner of the pan, then beat them into the mash with the mustard.
Gently fry the sliced green onions in the rest of the butter for 2 minutes, until just soft but still bright green. Fold them into the mash and serve.

title: Mutabbaq
steps: Heat a little oil in a frying pan and fry the crushed garlic and ginger, then add the ground beef and all the spices, the salt and the sugar. Cook until the meat is done, then let it cool.
Mix the meat with the egg, chopped tomato and chopped green onions.
Brush 2 sheets of filo with melted butter, put some filling in the middle, fold the pastry over it into a parcel and brush the seams with more butter. Repeat with the rest.
Fry the parcels in a little oil until golden on both sides and all the edges, or brush them with butter and bake at 350°F (180°C) for 10 to 15 minutes.

title: Nasi lemak
steps: Put the coconut milk, water, ginger paste, sliced ginger, a pinch of salt, the bay leaf and the rice in a saucepan, cover and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, until cooked.
Put the eggs in cold water, bring to a boil, take off the heat and leave them covered for 10 to 12 minutes. Cool, peel and halve them. Slice the cucumber.
Heat about 1 cup of oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the peanuts until lightly browned. Drain. Fry half of the anchovies until crisp and drain. Discard the oil.
Heat the 2 tbsp of oil and cook the chopped onion, garlic and shallots for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the chili powder mixed with a little water and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the rest of the anchovies for 5 minutes, then the sugar, tamarind and a pinch of salt, and simmer for about 5 minutes, until thick.
Serve the sauce over the rice, topped with the peanuts, fried anchovies, cucumber and eggs.

title: Nom Banh Chok – Cambodian Noodle Soup
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the minced garlic for about 1 minute, until golden.
Add the chicken pieces and cook for about 5 minutes, until opaque on all sides.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, stir in the fish sauce, salt and sugar and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles as the package says, drain and rinse them under cold water.
Divide the noodles between 4 bowls and ladle the broth and chicken over them. Top with bean sprouts, chopped mint and sliced chili, and serve with lime wedges.

title: Nordic smørrebrød with asparagus and horseradish cream
steps: Mix the crème fraîche, grated horseradish, lemon juice, salt and pepper and chill.
Fry the sliced shallots in a little oil over medium heat until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and salt lightly.
Blanch half of the asparagus (4 white and 4 green) in salted boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes, then cool it in ice water. Slice the rest thinly lengthwise to serve raw.
Heat the broiler. Butter the rye bread and toast it until golden and crisp.
Top each slice with both kinds of asparagus, drizzle with the horseradish cream, and sprinkle with the grated cheese, the crispy shallots and dill.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
steps: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Season the veal shanks and coat them in the flour, shaking off the extra.

Heat the oil and 1 tbsp of the butter in a wide, heavy ovenproof pot over medium-high heat. Brown the shanks for about 5 minutes on each flat side, in batches if needed. Set them aside and pour off the fat.

Melt the rest of the butter and cook the chopped onion, carrot, celery and fennel, seasoned, for about 6 minutes, until soft but not brown. Stir in 2 of the garlic cloves, the orange zest, marjoram and bay leaf for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the wine and boil until reduced by half, about 5 minutes. Add the broth and tomatoes and boil until there's about 1 cup of liquid, about 10 minutes.

Stand the shanks in the pot bone side up, pour over their juices, cover with parchment and the lid and braise in the oven for about 2 hours, turning them after 40 minutes, until the meat falls off the bone.

For the gremolata, mix the last garlic clove, finely chopped, with the parsley and lemon zest. Sprinkle half over the veal and return it to the oven uncovered for 15 minutes. Skim the sauce, season and serve with the rest of the gremolata.

title: Oyster Mushroom Soup
steps: Rinse and dry the mushrooms, remove the stems and cut them into thin strips.
Melt the butter in a small pot and cook the mushrooms for about 10 minutes, until they release their liquid.
Whisk the flour into the water until there are no lumps and add it to the pot with the salt and milk. Cook for 10 minutes more.
Mix the crushed garlic with the vinegar. Serve the soup with 1 to 2 tablespoons of the garlic vinegar and some pepper flakes.

title: Pa Amb Tomaquet (Bread with Tomato)
steps: Toast the bread slices in a toaster or a 400°F (200°C) oven until crisp and golden.
Rub each slice with a cut clove of garlic, then with a cut tomato half.
Drizzle with a little olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and serve warm.

title: Pad See Ew
steps: Soak or cook the noodles as the package says. Mix the dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and water in a small bowl.
Put the minced garlic and oil in a wok over high heat. When hot, add the sliced chicken and the Chinese broccoli stems and cook until the chicken is lightly golden.
Push everything to the side, crack in the egg and scramble it. It's fine if it sticks and chars a little.
Add the noodles, the broccoli leaves and the sauce and toss gently until the noodles are dark and the leaves have wilted. Serve right away.

title: Pad Thai
steps: Put the noodles in a large heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water for 4 minutes, then drain and rinse them under cold water.
Mix the juice of 4 of the limes with the cayenne, sugar and fish sauce.
Heat the oil and fry the shrimp until cooked. Add the sliced green onions and the noodles and toss.
Pour in the lime mixture, then stir in the bean sprouts and half of the chopped peanuts and cilantro. Cook for 1 minute, until hot.
Scatter with the rest of the peanuts and cilantro and serve with the last lime in wedges and sweet chili sauce.

title: Panang chicken curry (kaeng panang gai)
steps: For the curry paste, pound the dried and fresh chilies, shrimp paste, garlic, galangal, lemongrass, lime zest, coriander, cumin, nutmeg, peanuts and 1 tsp of salt into a rough paste. You can also pulse it in a food processor with 2 to 3 tbsp of the coconut milk. Keep any extra in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
Heat 2 to 3 tbsp of the thick coconut milk in a saucepan over medium-high heat. When it bubbles, stir in 1 to 2 tbsp of the paste for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the sliced chicken and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until it starts to brown, then the trimmed green beans.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, pour in the rest of the coconut milk, add 1 lime leaf and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes, until the chicken is cooked. Taste and adjust.
Stir in the basil, take it off the heat and serve with jasmine rice and the other lime leaf, finely sliced.

title: Pastel de Choclo
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan of water, bring to a boil, take off the heat and leave for 15 minutes. Cool, peel and chop them.
Heat a little oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the chopped onions and garlic with a pinch of salt, half of the paprika and some pepper for about 2 minutes.
Add the beef, the rest of the salt and paprika and more pepper, and cook for about 5 minutes, until mostly browned. Add the cooked, shredded chicken, the raisins, olives and eggs.

Blend the drained corn with the basil until smooth. Cook it in a saucepan with the butter over medium heat for 7 to 10 minutes, stirring, until thick. Stir in the milk, 2 tsp of sugar and a pinch of salt and cook for about 15 minutes more, until it's a thick paste.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread the meat in a baking dish, cover it with the corn paste, sprinkle with a little sugar and bake for about 20 minutes, until golden.

title: Pastel de Papas (Chilean Potato Pie)
steps: Cover the potatoes with salted water, bring to a boil and simmer for about 20 minutes, until tender.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onion for about 5 minutes, adding the garlic for the last minute. Stir in the chopped tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the beef and cook for about 10 minutes, until browned. Stir in the cheese, parsley and cayenne and season.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 2-quart baking dish. Drain the potatoes, mash them with the butter and salt, let them cool a little and stir in the beaten eggs.
Spread half of the potatoes in the dish, cover with the meat, then the rest of the potatoes.
Bake for about 40 minutes, until hot and lightly browned.

title: Paszteciki (Polish Pasties)
steps: Sift the flour and 1 tsp of the salt into a large bowl. Push 1 hard-boiled egg yolk through a fine sieve into it, add 1 raw egg and mix well. Beat in 5 tbsp of the butter, 1 tbsp at a time.
Knead the dough on a floured surface until smooth, wrap it and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onion and rutabaga for about 5 minutes, until soft. Grind or very finely chop them with the cooked beef.

Melt the rest of the butter, add the meat mixture and cook over low heat, stirring now and then, until dry and thick. Let it cool, then stir in 1 beaten egg and season with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Roll the dough into a 13 x 8-inch rectangle. Spoon the filling down the middle, wet the long edges and fold them over the filling, then fold in the ends.
Put it seam side down on a baking sheet, brush with the last egg, beaten, and bake for about 30 minutes, until golden. Cut it diagonally into 1 1/2-inch pieces.

title: Pierogi (Polish Dumplings)
steps: Melt half of the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook half of the chopped onion for about 5 minutes. Add the drained sauerkraut, cook for 5 minutes more, season and let it cool.
Melt the rest of the butter, cook the rest of the onion until translucent and stir it into the mashed potatoes. Season.
For the dough, beat the eggs with the sour cream. Sift the flour, salt and baking powder together, stir them in and knead on a floured surface until smooth and firm.

Roll half of the dough out 1/8 inch thick and cut 3-inch rounds. Put a small spoonful of potato filling in the middle of each, wet the edges, fold over and seal with a fork. Repeat with the rest of the dough and the sauerkraut filling.
Cook the pierogi in a large pot of lightly salted boiling water for 3 to 5 minutes, until they float. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.

title: Pilchard puttanesca
steps: Cook the pasta as the package says.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and cook the chopped onion, garlic and chili for 3 to 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the pilchards with their sauce, breaking up the fish with a spoon, then add the olives and cook for a few minutes more.
Drain the pasta and add it to the pan with 2 to 3 tbsp of the cooking water. Toss well and serve scattered with parmesan.

title: Piri-piri chicken and slaw
steps: Blend the chilies, garlic, ginger, oregano, coriander, paprika, 2 tbsp of the vinegar and the oil into a marinade. Rub it over the chicken and leave it for 1 hour at room temperature.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roast the chicken in a roasting pan for 1 hour 20 minutes, then let it rest under loose foil for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, for the slaw, mix the thinly sliced red onion, the grated carrots and beet and the shredded cabbage with the mayonnaise, yogurt, cumin seeds and the rest of the vinegar. Season.
Serve the chicken with the slaw.

title: Pisto con huevos
steps: Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole or cast-iron skillet over low heat. Add the chopped onions with a pinch of salt, cover and cook gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then. Add the garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the sliced peppers and cook, covered, over medium heat for about 5 minutes, until just tender.
Stir in the oregano, thyme, bay leaves and some salt and pepper. Add the diced zucchini and eggplant, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Make 4 hollows and carefully crack an egg into each. Cook over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, until the eggs are set but still a little soft. Scatter with parsley and serve.

title: Pollo en Salsa
steps: Chop the pepper, onion and tomato.
Heat a little olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion, garlic, tomato and pepper with the achiote paste, cumin, oregano, salt and pepper for about 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for about 2 minutes on each side.

Pour in the broth, cover and simmer over low heat for about 35 minutes, until the chicken is very tender. (In a pressure cooker, cook on high for 20 minutes.) Add salt if needed and serve with rice and beans.

title: Pomegranate salad
steps: Mix the olive oil, lemon juice, honey and thyme leaves in a large bowl and season well.
Add the lettuce, halved tomatoes, sliced green onions and chopped chili and toss.
Take the seeds out of the pomegranate over a bowl and remove any white pith.
Arrange the salad on a platter and scatter with the pomegranate seeds and crumbled feta.

title: Pork Cassoulet
steps: Heat the oven to 275°F (140°C). Heat the goose fat in a large ovenproof pan with a tight lid over high heat and brown the diced pork for a few minutes.
Lower the heat and add the sliced onion, whole garlic cloves, sliced carrot and fennel seeds. Cook gently for a few minutes to soften.
Pour in the vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pan. Add the broth, tomato paste and half of the rosemary and parsley. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes, then season.
Cover and cook in the oven for 2 hours, taking the lid off for the last hour. Stir now and then, and add the drained beans for the last 30 minutes.
Heat the broiler. Scatter the rest of the herbs and the breadcrumbs over the top, drizzle with a little oil and broil for 5 to 10 minutes, until golden. Serve with crusty bread and broccoli.

title: Portuguese barbecued pork (Febras assadas)
steps: Cut each pork tenderloin into 5 pieces. Put each piece in a plastic bag and pound it with a rolling pin into a thin cutlet.
Mix the wine, paprika, salt, pepper and the juice of half a lemon, add the pork and marinate for 20 to 30 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into 1-inch fries, soak them in cold water for 5 minutes, change the water and soak for 5 minutes more. Drain and pat dry.

Heat the oil in a deep pan to 265°F (130°C) and fry the potatoes in batches for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain. Heat the oil to 350°F (180°C) and fry them again for about 3 minutes, until crisp and golden. Drain and salt.
Rub the pork with olive oil and cook it on a very hot grill pan or barbecue for 1 minute on each side, in 2 batches.
Pile the fries on plates, top with the pork and its juices, and serve with mayonnaise and lemon wedges.

title: Portuguese prego with green piri-piri
steps: Rub the steaks with the cut garlic, put them in a bag with the olive oil, 1 tbsp of the vinegar and the parsley stalks, and pound them a few times with a rolling pin. Leave for 1 to 2 hours.
For the green sauce, blend the basil, jalapeño, green onions, sugar, the rest of the vinegar and 1 tbsp of water until smooth.
Heat a grill pan or frying pan until very hot. Brush off the garlic and parsley, season the steaks and sear them for 2 minutes on each side. Let them rest on a plate.
Toast the cut ciabatta halves and press them into the steak juices on the plate.
Slice the steaks and put them in the rolls with the green sauce and arugula.

title: Potato Gratin with Chicken
steps: Thinly slice the potatoes and boil them for 5 to 8 minutes, until firm but not soft.
Meanwhile, put the sliced onions in a baking dish with the olive oil and broth and cook in a 400°F (200°C) oven or on the stove until soft.
Drain the potatoes and spread them over the onions. Season and spoon over the crème fraîche to cover. Grate parmesan over the top and broil until golden.
Meanwhile, season the chicken and cook it in a frying pan for 5 to 7 minutes on each side, with the bacon, until cooked through.
Serve the gratin with the chicken and bacon, and with peas and spinach if you like.

title: Poulet Roti a l'Algerienne (Algerian Roast Chicken)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Mix the water, chopped onion, olive oil, vinegar, mustard, crushed garlic, black pepper, cayenne and salt in a roasting dish.
Add the chicken and turn it until well coated.
Roast for about 1 1/2 hours, basting now and then, until it reaches 165°F in the thickest part of the thigh.

title: Poutine
steps: Cut the potatoes into fries and pat them dry. Heat oil for deep-frying to 365°F (185°C).
Warm the gravy in a saucepan.
Fry the potatoes in batches for about 5 minutes, until golden, and drain on paper towels.
Pile the fries on a platter, scatter the cheese curds over them, ladle the hot gravy over the top and serve right away.

title: Provençal Omelette Cake
steps: Whisk 5 eggs in each of two bowls and season. Fry the sliced zucchini and green onions gently in the oil for about 10 minutes, until soft. Let them cool and stir them into one bowl.
Add the roasted, sliced peppers, the crushed garlic and the chopped chili to the other bowl and season.

Heat a little oil in an 8 to 9-inch non-stick frying pan. Pour in a third of the zucchini mixture and cook until set and lightly browned underneath, then flip it with a plate and cook the other side. Make 2 more, then 3 with the pepper mixture.
Beat the cream cheese with the milk until spreadable and stir in the chives, basil, salt and pepper.

Line a deep round cake pan the same size as the frying pan with plastic wrap. Layer the omelettes, alternating colors, with a thin layer of cheese between each. Cover and chill for a few hours or up to 24 hours.
Turn it out onto a plate, top with arugula, shaved parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil and black pepper, and cut into wedges.

title: Ramen Noodles with Boiled Egg
steps: Lower the egg into boiling water and cook for 6 1/2 to 7 minutes. Put it in ice water for 3 to 5 minutes, then peel it.
Bring the 2 cups of water to a boil and cook the noodles as the package says.
Stir in the soy sauce, chilli sauce, salt and pepper.
Pour into a bowl, top with the egg cut in half and the sliced green onions, and serve.

title: Rappie Pie
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and grease a 10 x 14-inch baking pan.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the chopped onions for about 5 minutes, then over low heat for about 40 minutes more, stirring, until very soft and dark brown.
Bring the broth to a boil in a large pot, add the chicken, lower the heat and simmer for about 20 minutes, until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
Peel and finely grate the potatoes, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean towel. Mix in the salt and pepper and enough hot broth to make a mixture like oatmeal.
Spread half of the potatoes in the pan, lay the sliced chicken over them, scatter with the onions and cover with the rest of the potatoes.
Bake for about 1 hour, until golden brown. Serve with a little of the reheated broth poured over each portion.

title: Raspeballer (Norwegian Potato Dumplings)
steps: Simmer the pork knuckle in water for about 3 hours, until the meat falls off the bone. Lift out the pork and keep the broth.
Meanwhile, boil half of the potatoes, peel them when cool and mash them well with no lumps. Peel and finely grate the rest and pat them dry with paper towels.
Mix the grated and mashed potatoes, then mix in the flour and salt with your hands.
Bring the pork broth to a very gentle simmer with the stock cubes (it mustn't boil hard). With a tablespoon dipped in cold water, shape smooth balls and drop them into the broth.

Simmer them for about 30 minutes, heating the sausage in the same pot. Meanwhile, boil the chopped rutabaga and carrots for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain and mash them with the cream, butter and nutmeg.
Serve the dumplings with the meat, the mash and chopped parsley.

title: Recheado Masala Fish
steps: Soak the dried chilies, ginger, garlic, pepper, cumin, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom and tamarind in the vinegar with the sugar, turmeric and a pinch of salt for 35 to 40 minutes.
Grind it all into a thick, smooth paste, adding a little more vinegar only if needed. It must stay thick to stick to the fish.
Rinse the mackerel, slit them open down the middle and cut a few slashes on top. Fill the slit and slashes with the paste and coat the fish all over. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a shallow pan and fry the fish until golden brown on both sides. Serve hot with salad, lime wedges and rice.

title: Ribollita
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large ovenproof pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrot, celery and garlic, season and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.

Heat the oven to 500°F (260°C). Add the drained beans, the tomatoes with their juice, the water, rosemary and thyme. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, breaking up the tomatoes.
Remove the herb stems and stir in the chopped kale. Taste and season.
Lay the bread over the top of the soup, scatter with the sliced red onion, drizzle with the rest of the oil and sprinkle with the parmesan.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the bread, onions and cheese are browned and crisp. Serve in bowls.

title: Rice and Beans
steps: Soak the dried kidney beans overnight, drain them, cover with fresh water and simmer for about 1 hour, until tender.
Add the rice, coconut milk, chopped onion, pepper and salt, with enough water to just cover everything.
Lay the whole Scotch bonnets on top, taking care not to burst them, and simmer covered for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Remove the peppers before serving.

title: Rigatoni with fennel sausage sauce
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pan with a lid and fry the sausages, cut into pieces, over medium-high heat for about 10 minutes, until browned. Set them aside.

Fry the chopped onion and fennel in the pan for 15 minutes, until soft and caramelized. Add the paprika, garlic and half of the fennel seeds for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and boil for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, sugar, 1/2 cup (100 ml) of water, the sausages and 1/2 tsp of salt. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, taking the lid off after 10 minutes, until thick. Stir in the olives and the rest of the fennel seeds.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water for 12 to 14 minutes, until al dente. Drain and stir in 1 tbsp of oil.
For the pesto, blend the pecorino, anchovy, the rest of the oil and 1 tbsp of water into a rough paste, then add the basil and pulse briefly.
Serve the pasta with the sauce and a spoonful of pesto on top.

title: Roast aubergine with goat's cheese & toasted flatbread
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Slice the eggplants, brush them with 1 tbsp of the oil, season and roast on a baking sheet for 20 minutes, until browned, adding the tomatoes for the last 5 minutes.
Tear the pita into pieces and toast it on another sheet for about 8 minutes, until crisp.
For the dressing, mix the vinegar, chopped mint, 1 chopped shallot, the chopped chili, the rest of the oil and some salt and pepper.
Put the eggplant, tomatoes, the other shallot, sliced, and the toasted pita in a bowl. Pour over the dressing, crumble the goat cheese on top and add the arugula.

title: Roast fennel and aubergine paella
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Toss the chopped fennel, eggplant, pepper and zucchini with a little olive oil, salt and pepper and roast for about 20 minutes, turning a couple of times, until golden and almost cooked.
Meanwhile, heat a little olive oil in a paella pan or large frying pan over low-medium heat and cook the chopped onion for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft.

Turn up the heat to medium, stir in the rice, paprika and saffron for 1 minute, then add the wine and reduce by half. Stir in two thirds of the broth and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring a couple of times.
Stir in the peas, season and gently mix in the roasted vegetables. Pour in the rest of the broth, lay lemon wedges on top, cover and cook for 10 minutes more.
Turn up the heat until you hear a slight crackle, to toast the bottom. Take it off the heat, let it sit for 5 minutes and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Roasted Eggplant With Tahini, Pine Nuts, and Lentils
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Heat 2 tbsp of olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the chopped carrots, celery and onion for about 4 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the lentils, bay leaves, water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, partly cover and cook for about 30 minutes, until tender, adding water if needed. Uncover, stir in the vinegar, let it reduce a little and season.

Meanwhile, cut the eggplants in half, score the flesh in a crisscross pattern and put them cut side up on a lined baking sheet. Brush each half with about 1 tbsp of oil, season and put a rosemary sprig on top. Roast for 25 to 35 minutes, until very tender and charred.
Toast the pine nuts in a little oil in a skillet for about 4 minutes, until golden. Thin the tahini with a little water, lemon or vinegar and salt to make a sauce.
Stir half of the parsley into the lentils, put them on a platter and lay the eggplant on top. Spoon the tahini sauce over, and sprinkle with the pine nuts and the rest of the parsley.

title: Rosemary braised red cabbage with kabanos
steps: Halve the cabbage, cut out the tough core and slice it thinly.

Put it in a large pan with everything else except the sausages: the oil, butter, sliced onion, vinegar, sugar, chopped chili, rosemary and diced apple. Add 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) of water and some salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring often and adding a little water if it gets dry.
Add the sausages, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, then uncover and cook for 10 minutes more. Serve with mashed or boiled potatoes.

title: Rosol (Polish Chicken Soup)
steps: Put the chicken in a large pot, cover with water and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, skimming off any foam so the broth stays clear.
For the last hour, add the onions, carrots, leek, celery and cabbage, the cloves, allspice, bay leaves, parsley, dill, pepper and salt.
Strain the broth. Pull the chicken off the bones in large chunks and slice the carrots.
Return the chicken and carrots to the broth and serve hot.

title: Roti john
steps: Mix the beef, chopped onion, eggs, chopped chili, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat a little oil in a pan or on a griddle and pour in the mixture.
Press the baguette, split open, cut side down on top and cook for about 2 minutes, until the egg sets.
Turn it over to crisp the bread a little. Add mayonnaise, cut it into pieces and serve.

title: Salmon Eggs Eggs Benedict
steps: For the hollandaise, whisk the lemon juice, 1 tsp of the vinegar and 3 of the egg yolks in a bowl until light and frothy. Set the bowl over a pan of simmering water and whisk until it thickens.
Gradually whisk in all but 1 tbsp of the butter, melted, until thick. If it looks like it's splitting, whisk it off the heat for a few minutes. Season and keep warm.

Bring a large pan of water to a boil, add the rest of the vinegar and lower the heat to a gentle simmer. Stir to make a slight whirlpool and slide in the other 4 eggs one at a time. Poach each for about 4 minutes and lift out with a slotted spoon.
Split, toast and butter the muffins. Put a couple of slices of salmon on each half, top with an egg and spoon over the hollandaise.

title: Salmon noodle soup
steps: Bring the broth to a boil in a large pan and stir in the curry paste.
Add the noodles and cook for 8 minutes, then the sliced mushrooms and the corn for 2 minutes more.
Add the salmon, cut into chunks, and cook for about 3 minutes, until cooked through.
Take it off the heat and stir in the lime juice, soy sauce and a pinch of sugar. Ladle into 4 bowls and sprinkle with cilantro.

title: Salmon Prawn Risotto
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pan and cook the chopped onion gently until soft, without browning.
Add the rice and stir to coat every grain. Pour in the wine and stir gently until absorbed.
Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed, for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender.
Meanwhile, broil the salmon and cook the shrimp and the asparagus until just done.
Stir the lemon juice and zest and some pepper into the risotto (the salmon is usually salty enough). Serve topped with the salmon, shrimp and asparagus and scattered with parmesan.

title: Saltfish and Ackee
steps: A day ahead, soak the salt cod overnight, changing the water a couple of times.
Drain it, cover with fresh water and bring to a boil. Drain again, add fresh water, bring to a boil and simmer for about 5 minutes. Drain and flake the fish, removing any skin or bones.
For the dumplings, mix the flour and suet with a pinch of salt and about 1 cup (250 ml) of water into a dough. Wrap and chill it.

Drain and rinse the ackee. Heat 1 tbsp of oil and fry the chopped onion until soft but not brown. Add the paprika, curry powder, allspice, hot sauce, salt, pepper and the sliced peppers and cook until the peppers are tender.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the cod, then gently stir in the ackee and simmer until you're ready to serve.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a frying pan. Shape the dough into plum-size balls and fry them until golden brown. Drain and serve with the saltfish and ackee.

title: Satee
steps: Blend the chopped onion, garlic, lemon juice, sugar, 3/4 cup of the soy sauce, the salt, coriander and 1 cup of the oil into a marinade.
Pour it over the cubed beef and marinate for a few hours (not overnight).
Thread the beef onto about 36 skewers.
Mix the rest of the oil and soy sauce in a shallow dish and roll each skewer in it.
Fry the skewers in a large pan, or cook them on a barbecue, turning them, until browned and cooked the way you like.

title: Sauerkraut and Fish Salad
steps: Hard-boil the egg, then peel and slice it. Toast the bread and cut it into pieces.
Whisk the oil with the honey and a pinch of salt into a dressing.
Mix the sauerkraut, egg, flaked fish and bread with the dressing and serve.

title: Sauerkraut pierogi
steps: For the crispy shallots, slice 2 of the shallots, toss them in a little flour and deep-fry them in hot oil (350°F/180°C) for about 1 minute, until golden. Drain on paper towels.

For the filling, heat 1/2 tbsp of the oil in a frying pan and gently fry the other 2 shallots, chopped, for 10 minutes. Add the sauerkraut and shredded cabbage and cook for 5 to 10 minutes, until soft. Season and let it cool completely.

For the dough, mix the egg and the rest of the oil with 1/2 cup (125 ml) of water, then gradually work in the flour. Knead on a floured surface until it stops sticking, wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out thinly on a well-floured surface and cut about 25 circles, 3 1/2 inches (9 cm) wide. Put 1 tsp of filling in the middle of each, fold into half-moons and pinch to seal.
Boil them in a large pan of salted water for about 2 minutes, until they float. Drain and serve with butter, sour cream and the crispy shallots.

title: Seafood fideuà
steps: Scrub the mussels, throwing away any with broken shells or that stay open when tapped, and pull off the beards. Peel the body of each shrimp, leaving the head and tail, and remove the vein.
Soak the saffron in 3 1/2 tbsp of hot water for 10 minutes. Crush the vermicelli into short pieces.

Heat the oil in a large, deep frying pan or paella pan and cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the pasta, and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until toasted brown. Stir in the paprika.

Stir in the monkfish and squid, cut into pieces, and the saffron with its water, and season. Spread it out evenly, pour in the hot stock, scatter with the chopped tomatoes, bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook over medium heat for 6 minutes.

Stir, then push the mussels into the pasta, hinge side down, and lay the shrimp on top. Cover and cook for 6 minutes more, until the mussels open, the shrimp are pink and the pasta is cooked. Simmer uncovered for 2 to 3 minutes to cook off most of the liquid.
Let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes, squeeze over the lemon and scatter with parsley.

title: Sesame Cucumber Salad
steps: Peel the cucumbers and cut them lengthwise into quarters. Scrape out the seeds if they're bitter, then cut them into 1/2-inch pieces.
Put them in a serving bowl, sprinkle with the salt and toss with the sesame oil, rice vinegar, torn basil and pepper flakes.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and serve.

title: Shakshuka
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan with a lid and soften the sliced onions, chili, garlic and chopped cilantro stalks for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and sugar and let them bubble for 8 to 10 minutes, until thick.
Make 4 hollows in the sauce with a spoon and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the eggs are done the way you like. Scatter with the cilantro leaves and crumbled feta and serve with crusty bread.

title: Shawarma chuck roast wrap
steps: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Stir all the spices, the salt, broth and lemon juice together in a heavy ovenproof pot.
Add the beef, turn it to coat and spoon some sauce over the top.
Cover and cook in the oven for about 3 1/2 hours, until very tender. (In a slow cooker, cook on low for 8 to 10 hours.)
Shred the beef with two forks, discarding any fat. Skim the fat off the sauce and mix the beef back in.
Fill the pitas with the beef and any toppings you like, fold them like a burrito and toast them in a hot grill pan.

title: Shrimp Chow Fun
steps: Soak the rice noodles until soft (or overnight for dried ones), then boil them as the package says and rinse them under cold water.
Mix the shrimp with the egg, a pinch of pepper, 1 tsp of the sesame oil, 1 tbsp of the cornstarch and 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok and stir-fry the shrimp until golden. Set them aside.
Add the last 1 tbsp of oil, the minced garlic and ginger, the sliced onion, bean sprouts and green onions, then the noodles.
Add the wine, oyster sauce, sugar, vinegar, the rest of the sesame oil, a pinch of pepper and the soy sauce, then return the shrimp.
Mix the rest of the cornstarch with 2 tbsp of water and stir in a little at a time until the sauce is as thick as you like.

title: Sichuan Style Stir-Fried Chinese Long Beans
steps: Trim the long beans and cut them into 3-inch pieces. Pat them dry.
Heat the peanut oil in a wok or large, deep pan over high heat. Stir-fry the beans for 5 to 7 minutes, until blistered and tender.
Push them to the side, add the dried chilies and Sichuan pepper and stir-fry for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Toss everything with the salt, sugar, sesame oil and a splash of soy sauce and serve right away.

title: Silken Tofu with Sesame Soy Sauce
steps: Drain the tofu and gently slide it out of the package onto a large plate.
Slice it into 1/2-inch slabs and gently push them so they fan out across the plate.
Drizzle with the soy sauce and the sesame paste, and garnish with the sliced green onion and sesame seeds.

title: Simple heart of palm & tomato salad
steps: Mix the sliced hearts of palm, halved tomatoes and sliced green onions.
Whisk the vinegar and olive oil together and drizzle it over the salad.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley, toss and serve.

title: Skillet Apple Pork Chops with Roasted Sweet Potatoes & Zucchini
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Dice the sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces, toss them on a baking sheet with a little oil, salt and pepper and roast on the top rack for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, core and thinly slice the apple, chop the garlic and quarter the lemon. Cut the zucchini into 1/2-inch half-moons and toss them on a second sheet with oil, salt and pepper.
Season the pork chops and cook them in a little oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, until cooked through. Set them aside.
Put the zucchini on the middle rack and roast both sheets for 12 to 15 minutes more, until browned.

Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in the pork pan, add the apple, season and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the broth and sugar, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, until thick and the apple is tender.
Take it off the heat and stir in the rest of the butter and a squeeze of lemon. Serve the pork with the apple sauce on top and the vegetables, with lemon squeezed over the zucchini.

title: Sledz w Oleju (Polish Herrings)
steps: Soak the salted herring in cold water for at least 1 hour, changing the water if they're very salty.
Drain them well and cut them into bite-size pieces.
Put them in a jar and cover with the oil, allspice, peppercorns and bay leaf. Close the jar.
Chill for 2 to 3 days before eating (it keeps for up to 2 weeks). Serve with finely chopped onion.

title: Slow-cooked, Wadadli-spiced Cubano pork belly
steps: Blend the olive oil, cilantro, parsley, oregano, mint, chilies, the juice of the oranges, limes and grapefruit, the garlic, cumin, allspice, salt and pepper into a marinade.
Lay the pork belly in a large dish, pour the marinade over it and rub it in everywhere. Cover and chill overnight.
Heat the oven to 275°F (140°C). Lift the pork into a large roasting dish, leaving most of the marinade behind, cover with foil and roast for 4 1/2 hours, basting it 3 or 4 times.
Uncover, turn the oven up to 350°F (180°C) and roast for 15 to 20 minutes more, until colored and soft enough to cut with a spoon.
Pull the pork apart and serve topped with more chopped cilantro and parsley.

title: Smoky Lentil Chili with Squash
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Slice the squash into thin crescents, drizzle with a little oil and salt and roast for 20 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until soft. Cool and cube it.
Meanwhile, rinse the lentils, cover them with water, bring to a boil and simmer uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes, until tender. Drain.

Heat the oil in a medium pot over low heat and cook the chopped onion and leek for about 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and coriander for a few minutes, then the paprika, cinnamon, chili powder, cocoa, salt and oregano.
Add the tomatoes, water and diced carrots and simmer, covered, for about 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender, stirring and adding water if needed.
Add the lentils and squash and cook for 10 minutes more.
For the cashew cream, soak the cashews in boiling water for at least 4 hours, drain and blend with about 1/2 cup of fresh water, a pinch of salt and the vinegar until creamy. Serve it on the chili.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
steps: Fry the chopped onions in the oil over fairly high heat for 3 to 4 minutes. Add the garlic and beef and fry until browned.
Add the sliced mushrooms and oregano and cook for a couple of minutes more.
Stir in the tomatoes, broth, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and seasoning. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water as the package says and drain it.
Stir the sauce into the spaghetti and serve with parmesan for sprinkling on top.

title: Spanish Tortilla
steps: Cook the sliced onion slowly in the oil and butter in a large non-stick frying pan over low heat for about 15 minutes, until soft but not brown.
Add the thinly sliced potatoes, cover and cook for 15 to 20 minutes more, stirring now and then, until soft.
Stir in 2 crushed garlic cloves, then the beaten eggs. Cover and cook gently for about 20 minutes, until the edges and bottom are golden and the top is set but still a little wobbly.
Slide it onto a plate, cover with another plate, flip it and slide it back into the pan for a few minutes to finish. Serve warm or cold, scattered with parsley.
On the side, toast slices of baguette, rub them with the rest of the garlic and top with grated tomato, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Spanish-style slow-cooked lamb shoulder & beans
steps: Mix the smoked paprika, rosemary and a large pinch of salt. Cut slashes all over the lamb and rub the mix in. If you have time, marinate it for up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole over medium-high heat and cook the chopped onions and carrots and the garlic cloves for 5 minutes.
Pour in the broth and bring to a boil. Nestle the lamb in the pan, cover and roast for 2 hours.
